title: Fix: wire free operators (+, -, *, /, %) through compound assigns

title: gate entire tests/lib/ subdirectory behind STURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE
description:
After sturm-eksf gated 7 named tests, the default-mode ctest still takes 18m14s wall-clock. Worker reported 9 more heavy QC simulation tests in tests/lib/ that each run 250-900 seconds:
- test_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot_adjoint: 900s
- test_square_mod_dsl: 884s
- test_mul_mod_inplace_dsl: 789s
- test_add_mod_dsl: 552s
- test_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot: 522s
- test_add_mod_inplace_dsl: 411s
- test_double_mod_dsl: 277s
- test_double_mod_dsl_adjoint: 76s
- test_double_mod_dsl_pool_drain: 36s

Sum ≈ 75 CPU-minutes — that's the bulk of the remaining wall-clock. They are all lib-level DSL roundtrip tests running 25-qubit state-vector QC simulations.

REQUIREMENT: in tests/CMakeLists.txt:153, wrap the existing 'add_subdirectory(lib)' line in 'if(STURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE) ... endif()'. Add a comment immediately above explaining: 'sturm-XXX: tests/lib/ holds DSL-level QC simulation tests (state-vector simulators, 25-qubit witnesses, multi-minute runs). Gate the entire subdirectory behind STURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE so the default ctest run stays fast.'

DO NOT touch the contents of tests/lib/CMakeLists.txt — gating the add_subdirectory call is sufficient. The seven add_test() blocks already gated by sturm-eksf inside tests/lib/CMakeLists.txt become double-gated, which is fine.

VERIFICATION:
1. Default OFF: `cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/clang++-17` then `ctest --test-dir build -N | grep -c 'test_.*_dsl'` should drop dramatically (from ~30 to a small number — most _dsl tests live in tests/lib/).
2. ON: `cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/clang++-17 -DSTURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE=ON` re-registers everything in tests/lib/.
3. Time default mode: `time ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --parallel 6`. Target: under 5 min wall-clock (the prior run was 18m14s; with tests/lib/ excluded most of the heavy sim cost is gone).
4. Confirm no test failures in default-mode run that were NOT failing before.
5. Leave the build configured with STURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE=OFF (default).

ACCEPTANCE: default ctest does not register any tests/lib/ test; reconfiguring with -DSTURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE=ON re-registers them; default-mode wall-clock is dramatically faster (target: under 5 min).

title: gate remaining slow ctests behind STURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE
description:
Even with cmake_modular_pow_* gated (sturm-dp9a), the default ctest run still has multi-minute / multi-hour outliers. The two test_mul_mod_dsl* tests carry TIMEOUT 3600 (intentional 25-qubit state-vector QC simulations, 30+ min each on dev box). Several other tests run > 5s individually or in 12-instance parameter sweeps and are not needed in the default per-iteration run.

REQUIREMENTS — gate each of these add_test() registrations behind `if(STURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE) ... endif()` (the option already exists from sturm-dp9a):

A. tests/lib/CMakeLists.txt
   - line ~418: add_test(NAME test_mul_mod_dsl ...) + matching set_tests_properties (line ~419-421, includes TIMEOUT 3600). Leave the add_executable+target_* lines unconditional so the binary still builds (or also gate them for build-time savings; either is acceptable but pick one and stick with it).
   - line ~447: add_test(NAME test_mul_mod_dsl_adjoint ...) + matching set_tests_properties (line ~448-450, includes TIMEOUT 3600).
   - line ~810: add_test(NAME test_pow_mod_xval ...) + matching set_tests_properties.

B. tests/control/CMakeLists.txt:95
   - add_test(NAME test_add_mod_when_lift ...) + matching set_tests_properties.

C. transpiler/tests/CMakeLists.txt
   - line ~2022: add_test(NAME test_plugin_nested ...) + set_tests_properties (already inside an if(STURM_PLUGIN_CLANGXX_BIN AND STURM_PLUGIN_OBJDUMP_BIN) block — gate the inner add_test calls).
   - line ~3338: add_test(NAME test_qram_e2e_real ...) and any matching set_tests_properties.
   - line ~3392: add_test(NAME test_qint_alias_subst_e2e ...) — CAUTION: this likely registers 12 invocations via a foreach. Gate the foreach loop OR gate each add_test inside it.

For each gated test, in the comment immediately above, append a single line: '# sturm-XXX: gated behind STURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE (cost: <observed>s).' (where XXX is this issue's id).

VERIFICATION (run all):
1. Default OFF: `cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/clang++-17` then `ctest --test-dir build -N | grep -cE '(test_mul_mod_dsl|test_mul_mod_dsl_adjoint|test_pow_mod_xval|test_add_mod_when_lift|test_plugin_nested|test_qram_e2e_real|test_qint_alias_subst_e2e)'` should be 0.

3. Time the default-mode run END-TO-END: `time ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure --parallel 6`. Expect dramatically faster wall-clock (no individual test > ~5s, target total under ~2 min).
4. After verification, leave the build configured with the option OFF (default).

Do NOT attempt to fix any pre-existing failures in the default-mode run that are unrelated to the gating change — report them separately.

ACCEPTANCE: default ctest does not register any of the listed tests; reconfiguring with -DSTURM_FULL_TEST_SUITE=ON re-registers all of them; default-mode wall-clock for the full suite is dramatically faster (target: under 2 min).

title: transpiler plugin GPL-license loader env issue under clang++-17 build
description:
After reconfiguring the build with -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/clang++-17 (to enable -Xclang plugin args used by add_quantum_executable), the loaded plugin libsturm-transpile-plugin.so triggers 'cc1: fatal error: plugin libsturm-transpile-plugin.so is not licensed under a GPL-compatible license: undefined symbol plugin_is_GPL_compatible'.

This cascades through ~48 ctest entries in the full gate: test_plugin_load, pm4_smoke_dlopen*, pm4_two_plugins_independent*, build_example_* (12), transpiler_*_injected (12), transpiler_idempotent_* (12). NOT D0-related — a build-env / plugin source issue.

Likely root cause: the plugin TU is missing 'extern "C" int plugin_is_GPL_compatible;' which g++/clang plugin loaders require. Could also be a linkage flags issue (-shared, -fPIC, position-independent globals).

REPRO: ctest --test-dir build -R '^(test_plugin_load|pm4_smoke_dlopen|build_example_|transpiler_)' --output-on-failure --parallel 2

ACCEPTANCE: full gate (with user exclusion regex) executes the plugin-loading targets without 'plugin_is_GPL_compatible' undefined-symbol failure.

title: header-cycle regression: qint_fwd.hpp uses sturm::frontend::qint before qint_alias.hpp defines it
description:
When qint_alias.hpp is the FIRST header included (e.g. tests/qtypes/test_qint_alias.cpp:22), the include cycle qint_alias.hpp -> qint_fwd.hpp -> qint_alias.hpp (re-entry blocked by pragma once) returns to qint_fwd.hpp BEFORE class sturm::frontend::qint has been parsed, so line 36 'using qint = ::sturm::frontend::qint;' fails with: 'frontend in namespace sturm does not name a type'.

REPRO: cmake --build build --parallel 2 --target test_qint_alias  (build/CMakeCache.txt CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/c++ g++15)

ROOT CAUSE: sturm-65rs.6 (B1) repointed sturm::qint to sturm::frontend::qint and reordered qint_fwd.hpp per PRD §4.2 step (1)-(4). The order is correct ONLY when qint_fwd.hpp is the entry point; when qint_alias.hpp is the entry point, step (4) (alias definition) is reached before qint_alias.hpp finishes defining frontend::qint.

WHY MISSED: B0 (sturm-65rs.5) header-cycle audit asserted the cycle was safe. B1 added tests/packaging/test_qint_resolution.cpp, but that file does NOT include qint_alias.hpp directly — it goes through sturm/prelude.hpp / qint_fwd.hpp. test_qint_alias.cpp DOES include qint_alias.hpp directly (line 22) and was not built in B0/B1's targeted ctest subset.

FIX OPTIONS (for owner to choose):
(a) Move 'using sturm::qint = sturm::frontend::qint;' OUT of qint_fwd.hpp into a separate qint_alias_finalize.hpp included AFTER qint_alias.hpp's class definition completes.
(b) Forward-declare class sturm::frontend::qint in qint_fwd.hpp before line 36 (sufficient for the using-declaration since it's a type-alias, not a use).
(c) Make qint_alias.hpp self-contained (don't include qint_fwd.hpp; declare its own forward decl of qint_t<W>) so qint_fwd.hpp -> qint_alias.hpp is no longer a cycle.

ACCEPTANCE: cmake --build build --parallel 2 --target test_qint_alias compiles; test_qint_alias passes; the 50+ fixture/test files that include various headers in any order all compile.

title: test_transpile_consumer fails to link after QRAM matcher/emitter sources added (sturm-ddgo regression)
description:
Full-suite gate after sturm-ddgo (commit 242ffd4) is RED at link time. The QRAM matcher/emitter sources were added to the `sturm-transpile` and `sturm-transpile-plugin` libraries in `transpiler/CMakeLists.txt`, but `transpiler/tests/CMakeLists.txt` builds `test_transpile_consumer` by compiling `transpile_consumer.cpp` directly (not by linking against `sturm-transpile`). The new code in `transpile_consumer.cpp` references symbols from the newly-added sources, so the test binary fails to link.

## Reproduce

```bash
cmake --build build --target test_transpile_consumer --parallel 6
```

## Linker errors

```
CMakeFiles/test_transpile_consumer.dir/__/src/transpile_consumer.cpp.o:
undefined reference to `sturm::transpile::register_qram_subscript_matcher(clang::ast_matchers::MatchFinder&, std::vector<sturm::transpile::QramSubscriptHit, ...>&)'
undefined reference to `sturm::transpile::register_qram_subscript_assign_matcher(...)'
undefined reference to `sturm::transpile::register_qram_subscript_expr_matcher(...)'
undefined reference to `sturm::transpile::emit_qram_replacements(...)'
undefined reference to `sturm::transpile::emit_qram_assign_replacements(...)'
undefined reference to `sturm::transpile::emit_qram_expr_replacements(...)'
```

Call sites: `transpiler/src/transpile_consumer.cpp:293, 295, 297, 1118, 1121, 1123`.

## Scope

Fix `transpiler/tests/CMakeLists.txt` so `test_transpile_consumer` resolves the QRAM symbols. Two viable approaches:
1. Add the six new sources (`matcher_qram_subscript{,_assign,_expr}.cpp` + `qram_emitter{,_assign,_expr}.cpp` + `width_inference.cpp`) to the `test_transpile_consumer` target's source list — matches the existing pattern of compiling `transpile_consumer.cpp` directly into the test.
2. Refactor the test to link against the `sturm-transpile` library instead of recompiling sources directly. Larger blast radius — defer unless option 1 turns out to be ugly.

Prefer option 1 unless there's a compelling reason; the test pattern of compiling consumer sources directly is established.

## Acceptance

- `cmake --build build --parallel 6` succeeds (no link errors).
- `ctest --output-on-failure --parallel 6` produces no NEW failures vs. the known `STURM_AUTO_UNCOMPUTE=OFF` baseline.
- `test_transpile_consumer` passes its own tests.

## Threading

Every cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocation MUST be capped at 6 parallel threads (`--parallel 6`, `-j6`). No exceptions.

## Context

Introduced by sturm-ddgo (commit 242ffd4). The worker's targeted tests (`ctest -L qram-subscript --parallel 6`) were green because they don't build `test_transpile_consumer`. The full-suite gate caught this.

title: D1: QRAM_read runtime stub (counter-mode)
description: Stand up the runtime entry-point so emitter output compiles and the counter-mode sink (B1a) records the operation; semantics defined by D0a/D0b (PRD §8, M4). Production: include/sturm/qram/qram_read.hpp (≤200 LoC) with templated declarations covering std::array<qint_t<W>,N>, qint_t<W>[N] (decay to pointer), and qint_t<W>* per D0a; adjoint registration via STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT per P9c with the name from D0d. title: C1: matcher_qram_subscript.{hpp,cpp} (v1 matcher)
description: Recognise exactly the v1 shape qint b = a[i]; for the three containers in PRD §7. Produce a hit vector consumed by D2. Production: transpiler/src/matcher_qram_subscript.{hpp,cpp} (each ≤300 LoC). Mirrors matcher_modular_op.cpp style: register_qram_subscript_matcher(MatchFinder&, Hits&) pushes one QramSubscriptHit per match. Hit carries: VarDecl for b; container expr a with discriminated kind {StdArray, CArray, Pointer}; index expr i; inferred width W via B1; source-ranges. Discriminator: the index sub-expression contains an ImplicitCastExpr of CK_UserDefinedConversion whose conversion function is qint::operator size_t. Container detection: CXXOperatorCallExpr on std::array::operator[] for std::array; ArraySubscriptExpr for C-array and pointer (distinguished by base expression type). Tests: transpiler/tests/test_matcher_qram_subscript.cpp (≤300 LoC) — three positives (one per container shape) producing exactly one hit each with correct kind tag; negatives for classical size_t index (zero hits), existing-target b (zero hits — E1's job), subscript inside larger expression (zero hits — E1's job). title: B1: width inference (transpiler/src/width_inference.{hpp,cpp})

Three rules in the order fixed by D0c: (1) RHS-driven — if initializer is a subscript on a container of qint_t<W>, return W; (2) future-reserved annotation form qint<W> (PRD §6c) gated behind kAllowAnnotation=false in v1, fires a 'reserved' diagnostic and falls through; (3) global default (32 or 64 per D0c) lives in a single named constant. title: Factor depth-1 lift helper into include/sturm/control/lift.hpp
STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT must key on NTTP to allow same-signature forwards
description:
REGRESSION: commits d3d060f (sturm-le6w / LO-1d lib_or_dsl adjoint) and 98b7895 (sturm-eum8 / LO-1c lib_c_AND_dsl adjoint) both call STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT on function templates with identical signature void(*)(BitProxy&, BitProxy&, BitProxy&). The current macro (include/sturm/routines/invert.hpp) keys the adjoint_of<> trait specialization on decltype(&fn) — the function-pointer TYPE — so both specializations collide. Any TU that pulls in both logic_dsl.hpp and c_and_dsl.hpp (e.g. tests/backend/test_m8_template_dsl.cpp via compare_dsl.hpp) fails to build with 'redefinition of adjoint_of<void (*)(sturm::BitProxy&, sturm::BitProxy&, sturm::BitProxy&)>'.

ROOT CAUSE: invert.hpp's trait is keyed on fn-pointer type, not value. Two function-template instantiations with the same signature cannot both register.

SCOPE:
- Redesign include/sturm/routines/invert.hpp so the adjoint_of<> trait is keyed on a non-type template parameter (auto Fn) — the function-pointer VALUE, not its type. Project is C++20, NTTP for function pointers is supported.
- Update STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT macro so the expansion becomes: template <> struct adjoint_of<&::fn> { static constexpr auto value = &::adj; }; keyed on the literal pointer value.
- Migrate the invert() call shape. Current call: invert(&fn)(args). Candidate replacement: invert<&fn>()(args). Alternatively keep invert(&fn) as a constexpr overload that forwards to invert<Fn>() via consteval/constant-evaluation if that round-trips cleanly; the NTTP key is what matters. Pick whichever preserves the most call sites.
- Migrate every existing call site. Audit: grep -rn 'sturm::invert' include/ tests/ src/. At minimum tests/test_invert.cpp (~20 sites), tests/lib/test_or_dsl_adjoint.cpp, tests/lib/test_c_and_dsl_adjoint.cpp, tests/lib/test_div_mod_dsl_adjoint.cpp, plus any lossy-rewrite emitter call sites already landed.
- Every test that currently passes must continue to pass, AND tests/backend/test_m8_template_dsl.cpp must build cleanly with both c_and_dsl.hpp and logic_dsl.hpp registrations live.
- All build/test commands capped at --parallel 6 / -j6. No exceptions.

ACCEPTANCE:
- cmake --build build --parallel 6 succeeds.
- ctest --parallel 6 -L lossy-reversibility passes (4 tests).
- ctest --parallel 6 -R 'test_m8_template_dsl|test_invert' passes.
- Macro docstring in invert.hpp updated to explain NTTP keying and why type-based keying is insufficient (so the next author does not regress).

BLOCKS: all remaining LO-* issues that register or invert() adjoints, i.e. LO-1a (sturm-735v), LO-1b already landed but its test must stay green, LO-2a..e, LO-3a..c, LO-4, LO-5. This issue is a hard prerequisite — the autopilot is paused on its resolution.

title: Correct lossy compound assignments (&=, |=, *=, /=, %=) inside WHEN
description: qint_t::operator &=, |=, *=, /=, %= currently end with an unconditional release(old_A) + pointer relabel to a freshly computed result register. Correct when uncontrolled, but inside WHEN(ctrl) it silently zeroes A in the ctrl=|0> branch because the compute gates are lifted to controlled form while the relabel runs unconditionally. Fix: replace the relabel tail with a control-stack branch: uncontrolled keeps the zero-gate relabel; controlled emits a per-bit Fredkin via the existing a^=b;b^=a;a^=b idiom (auto-lifted by BitProxy / emit_CX_lifted) and leaves the now-garbage res_idx[] qubits allocated. Because these ops are lossy on A, full uncomputation is impossible without extra state; this session accepts the leak and exposes the leaked registers via a new detail::garbage_registry so a future transpiler pass can consume them. ^=, +=, -= are already genuinely in-place under WHEN (gates on original qubits via BitProxy); they only need regression tests. See plan at ~/.claude/plans/okay-if-no-questions-logical-pascal.md.

title: PM1-0 — De-risking spike: nested CompilerInvocation inside a Clang plugin
description:
Phase M item 1 (in-memory transpile) de-risking spike. Before committing to the plugin architecture, prove the nested-invocation shape works end-to-end on a trivial case on a throwaway branch.

Tasks:
- Write a minimal PluginASTAction that prints 'hello from sturm plugin' and runs an EmitObjAction on an in-memory buffer containing the ORIGINAL source (no rewrites yet). Confirm it produces a valid .o that links.
- Verify CompilerInvocation clone inherits -O2, -I<path>, -D<macro> correctly by toggling each and inspecting the nested invocation's CompilerInvocation::print().
- Verify InMemoryFileSystem + OverlayFileSystem composition exposes the rewritten buffer to the nested parse while keeping real headers on disk reachable.

Deliverable: working plugin + CMake integration snippet + one-paragraph write-up in the bd issue notes. If the spike fails or reveals a blocker on our LLVM 17-19 target range, file a rollback to Strategy 3 (pipe-to-stdin) and re-consult.

Gate: do not start PM1-1 until PM1-0 is green.
notes:
Spike (PM1-0) landed green on llvm-17 / ubuntu on 2026-04-19.

Three gates all pass (ctest -R spike_nimr, exit 0):

  gate1 — The PluginASTAction (class SpikeAction, actionType
    ReplaceAction) registered as "sturm-spike" loads via
    `clang++-17 -Xclang -load -Xclang <.so> -Xclang -plugin -Xclang
    sturm-spike`, prints "hello from sturm plugin" to stderr on
    ExecuteAction, and runs a nested EmitObjAction on the original
    in-memory main-file buffer. The emitted .o links with clang++ and
    the resulting binary runs and returns 0.
  gate2 — Cloning the parent invocation via
    `std::make_shared<CompilerInvocation>(getCompilerInstance().
    getInvocation())` inherits -O2, -I<path>, and -D<macro> unchanged.
    Verified by dumping the cloned invocation via
    `cloned->getCC1CommandLine()` (Clang 17 has no `.print()` API —
    the issue said 'print()' but the getCC1CommandLine flag list is
    semantically equivalent and sufficient for the gate). -O2,
    the absolute path of -I, and the macro identifier all appear
    between the '=== cloned CompilerInvocation ===' bookends.
  gate3 — The nested frontend sees the in-memory buffer via an
    `llvm::vfs::OverlayFileSystem` that pushes an
    `llvm::vfs::InMemoryFileSystem` on top of
    `llvm::vfs::getRealFileSystem()`. A main file that
    #includes <cstdio> AND <cstdlib> compiles cleanly through the
    overlay — system headers resolve via the RealFileSystem branch
    while the main source is shadowed by the in-memory entry.

API / version findings for Phase M1:

  * `CompilerInvocation::print()` does NOT exist in Clang 17 (issue
    description is slightly wrong). The canonical dump call is
    `getCC1CommandLine()` returning `std::vector<std::string>`.
    Phase M1 (sturm-gnmo / sturm-bkcr) should update the plan text
    to match.
  * The plugin .so must NOT re-export LLVM symbols or clang aborts
    with "Option 'debug-counter' registered more than once!" when
    the outer driver loads it. On Linux,
    `-Wl,--exclude-libs,ALL` combined with MODULE (dlopen) linkage
    and the shared libclang-cpp / libLLVM (not static per-component
    archives) is sufficient; no macOS equivalent needed (tested on
    Linux only — macOS verification deferred to sturm-gnmo since
    the spike box is Linux).
  * `PluginASTAction::ExecuteAction()` must chain to the base-class
    `ExecuteAction()` BEFORE the nested invocation runs so the
    parent AST walk / diagnostic state settles.  Without the chain,
    the parent parse never completes and the nested frontend sees
    a half-finished invocation.
  * The plugin had to call `child.createFileManager(overlay);
    child.createSourceManager(child.getFileManager());` explicitly
    — the nested `CompilerInstance` does not reuse the parent's
    FileManager, so leaving those default-null would have every
    #include miss.
  * Driving the plugin via the `clang++` DRIVER (not `-cc1`) is the
    only sane invocation for PM1 example CTests; -cc1 requires
    spelling out every -internal-isystem path, which varies
    across distros.  Phase M1's add_quantum_executable (PM1-5)
    should mirror the driver-mode -Xclang pattern.

Conclusion: no blocker on LLVM 17. The nested-invocation shape works
as planned and Phase M1 (PM1-1..PM1-9) is cleared to proceed. No
rollback to Strategy 3 (pipe-to-stdin) needed.

Spike artefacts live under transpiler/spike_nimr/ on a throwaway
branch spike/sturm-nimr-nested-plugin; nothing wires into the main
sturm-transpile binary. The branch will be discarded once PM1-3
(sturm-gnmo) lands the production plugin.

title: dump mode: parse fails on SDK 26 libc++ headers under clang-17
description:
STURM_TRANSPILE_MODE=dump configures and links the standalone sturm-transpile binary against Homebrew llvm@17, then runs libTooling parses against MacOSX26.sdk's libc++ headers. SDK 26 libc++ uses Clang >=19 builtins (__builtin_clzg, __builtin_ctzg, _LIBCPP_NO_SPECIALIZATIONS, __is_nothrow_convertible builtin), so the parse fails with 12 errors before the rewrite even starts.

Repro:
  rm -rf build_mac
  cmake -S . -B build_mac -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DSTURM_TRANSPILE_MODE=dump \
    -DLLVM_DIR=$(brew --prefix llvm@17)/lib/cmake/llvm \
    -DClang_DIR=$(brew --prefix llvm@17)/lib/cmake/clang
  cmake --build build_mac --target example_or_circuit --parallel 6
  # → 12 errors of the shape:
  #   .../is_convertible.h:32:99: error: '_Tp' does not refer to a value
  #   .../countr.h:28:10: error: use of undeclared identifier '__builtin_ctzg'
  #   .../countl.h:28:10: error: use of undeclared identifier '__builtin_clzg'

Plugin mode is unaffected because that path uses /usr/bin/c++ (Apple Clang) which speaks its own SDK; only dump mode runs Clang-17 against SDK-26 libc++.

Fix:
- Promote LLVM_INSTALL_PREFIX (set by find_package(LLVM) in transpiler/CMakeLists.txt) to a CACHE INTERNAL variable so cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake (included from root) can reach it.
- In _sturm_add_quantum_executable_dump (cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake:486-491), append to _xa_args when LLVM_INSTALL_PREFIX/include/c++/v1 exists:
    --extra-arg=-nostdinc++
    --extra-arg=-cxx-isystem<prefix>/include/c++/v1
  This routes the libTooling parse through llvm@17's bundled libc++ (which DOES match the parser version), bypassing the SDK headers.
- Guard with EXISTS so non-mac / different llvm distributions degrade gracefully.

Acceptance:
- After the fix, 'rm -rf build_mac && cmake -S . -B build_mac -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSTURM_TRANSPILE_MODE=dump -DLLVM_DIR=$(brew --prefix llvm@17)/lib/cmake/llvm -DClang_DIR=$(brew --prefix llvm@17)/lib/cmake/clang && cmake --build build_mac --target example_or_circuit --parallel 6' succeeds.
- build_mac/sturm_gen/examples/or_circuit.cpp is produced and carries the '// AUTO-GENERATED by sturm-transpile' header.
- Plugin mode still passes a clean rebuild (no regression in the default path).

title: Fix per-source plugin dylib dependency in add_quantum_executable (Ninja race)
description:
On Ninja, building any add_quantum_executable target in plugin mode without first building the plugin races: the example's .cpp compile (which loads libsturm-transpile-plugin.dylib via -fplugin=...) is scheduled in parallel with the plugin's own .o compiles, so the dylib does not exist when clang dlopens it.

Repro:
  rm -rf build_mac
  cmake -S . -B build_mac -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DSTURM_TRANSPILE_MODE=plugin \
    -DLLVM_DIR=$(brew --prefix llvm@17)/lib/cmake/llvm \
    -DClang_DIR=$(brew --prefix llvm@17)/lib/cmake/clang
  cmake --build build_mac --target example_or_circuit --parallel 6
  # → error: unable to load plugin '.../libsturm-transpile-plugin.dylib': dlopen ... no such file

Root cause: cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake:297-303 uses add_dependencies(${target} ${_sturm_aliased}). With the Ninja generator, target-level add_dependencies only gates the link step of ${target} on the plugin target's outputs; it does not gate per-source .o compiles. -fplugin=<path> is consumed at parse time, so each user .cpp.o compile must depend on the plugin DYLIB FILE, not just the plugin target.

Fix:
- In _sturm_add_quantum_executable_plugin (cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake), inside the per-source foreach, append the plugin's dylib file to OBJECT_DEPENDS of each abs_src:
    set_property(SOURCE "${abs_src}" APPEND PROPERTY OBJECT_DEPENDS
        "$<TARGET_FILE:sturm::transpile-plugin>")
  Resolve the ALIAS first if OBJECT_DEPENDS rejects ALIAS targets — use $<TARGET_FILE:${_sturm_aliased}> or the IMPORTED location for find_package consumers.
- Keep the existing target-level add_dependencies for the IMPORTED-target / link-step path.
- Keep PLUGINS entries (the runtime-loaded plugins) on OBJECT_DEPENDS as well so a touch on one of them re-triggers the parse.

Acceptance:
- After cmake -G Ninja configure, running 'cmake --build build_mac --target example_or_circuit --parallel 6' from a clean build_mac succeeds without a prior 'cmake --build ... --target sturm-transpile-plugin' step.
- 'cmake --build build_mac --parallel 6' (default target) on a clean build_mac succeeds.
- Touching transpiler/src/plugin.cpp and rebuilding example_or_circuit recompiles or_circuit.cpp.o (file-level invalidation now works, replacing the manageable-limitation note in cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake:383-393).

title: test_cmake_plugins breaks dump-mode configure
description: tests/transpiler/CMakeLists.txt:29 unconditionally calls `add_subdirectory(test_cmake_plugins)`. That sub-project's CMakeLists.txt (line 99) calls `add_quantum_executable(... PLUGINS ...)`, which the helper rejects at configure time when STURM_TRANSPILE_MODE != plugin (cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake:174). Net effect: `-DSTURM_TRANSPILE_MODE=dump` cannot configure at all because of a single test that is plugin-mode-specific by design. title: Dump-mode missing -I${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/include
description: cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake:482-486 (dump-mode add_custom_command) forwards -I${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/include but not -I${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/include. The latter is where `<sturm/version.hpp>` lands (top-level CMakeLists.txt configure_file from include/sturm/version.hpp.in). Plugin mode inherits this via the normal compile rule; dump mode invokes the standalone sturm-transpile binary directly and needs the path spelled out as --extra-arg. Without it, every dump-mode build of any source that includes <sturm/sturm.hpp> fails with `'sturm/version.hpp' file not found`. Sandbox-verified: adding the second -I makes example_or_circuit build cleanly in dump mode and emits build_dump/sturm_gen/examples/or_circuit.cpp. Fix already applied in commit-pending edit.

title: Add precompiled headers to transpiler targets
description: Each of ~50 transpiler TUs reparses heavy clang/llvm headers (clang/AST/*, ASTMatchers, RecursiveASTVisitor, etc.) from scratch — measured top headers: Expr.h/Decl.h/ASTContext.h hit by 49/51 TUs, ASTMatchFinder.h by 48/51, SourceLocation.h by 44/51. description:

title: C1 matcher does not fire against real std::array / qint_alias.hpp
description:
The QRAM C1 matcher (transpiler/src/matcher_qram_subscript.cpp, sturm-u9ge.12) recognises `qint b = a[i];` against the hermetic test fixtures (transpiler/tests/fixtures/qram_read_std_array.cpp + the embedded stub in transpiler/tests/test_qram_e2e.cpp), but does NOT fire when the same source line is compiled against the production headers (real `std::array` from `<array>` + real `frontend::qint` from include/sturm/qtypes/qint_alias.hpp + real `qint_t<W>` from include/sturm/qtypes/qint_core.hpp).

Reproduce:
  examples/qram_demo.cpp:demo_natural_syntax() contains:
    qint i = 2;
    std::array<sturm::qint_t<4>, 4> a = { ... };
    qint b = a[i];
  Build: `cmake --build build --target example_qram_demo --parallel 6`
  Inspect: build/sturm_gen/examples/qram_demo.cpp — the line is unchanged
  (should be: `sturm::qint_t<4> b; ::sturm::QRAM_read(a, i, b);`).
  Runtime: measurement_count() reports 2 after the call (1 from the
  `a[i]` operator size_t UDC, 1 from the converting ctor body); should
  be 0 if the rewrite fired.

Probable cause: the matcher pattern
  varDecl(
    hasType(hasCanonicalType(hasDeclaration(cxxRecordDecl(hasName(\"qint\"))))),
    hasInitializer(ignoringImplicit(
      cxxConstructExpr(hasArgument(0, ignoringParenImpCasts(subscript))))))
or the upstream `index_has_qint_udc` walker depends on AST shape details
(template-parameter type — the production `qint_t<W>` uses
`template<std::size_t W>` while the fixture stub uses `template<int W>`;
real `std::array::operator[]` likely has more wrapping ICE/CXXFunctionalCast
nodes than the hermetic stub) that differ between the hermetic fixture
and the real headers.

Scope:
- Investigate the AST shape difference using `clang -Xclang -ast-dump=json`
  on examples/qram_demo.cpp and compare to the fixture transpile.
- Adjust the matcher pattern OR the UDC walker to handle the production AST
  without breaking the fixture-based tests.
- Update tests/qram/test_qram_e2e.cpp (or add a new e2e test) to ALSO
  compile against the real headers, not just the hermetic stub, so this
  gap is caught by ctest.
- Update examples/qram_demo.cpp [A] section message to assert the rewrite
  fires (measurement_count() == 0 post-call).

Related: H1 (sturm-u9ge.6) and H4 (sturm-u9ge.9) matchers likely have the
same gap — verify and fix all three at once if so.

Threading: every cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocation MUST be capped at -j6.

title: frontend::qint converting constructor from qint_t<W>
description:
The C1 matcher rewrites the source line

    qint b = a[i];   // a is std::array<qint_t<W>, N> or similar

into

    sturm::qint_t<W> b; ::sturm::QRAM_read(a, i, b);

before clang compiles. But the ORIGINAL line must PARSE first so the transpiler plugin can walk the AST and identify the rewrite site. Today, the production frontend::qint at include/sturm/qtypes/qint_alias.hpp has no converting constructor from sturm::qint_t<W>, so the line fails to parse against the production header (the test fixtures get around this with a hermetic frontend::qint stub — see transpiler/tests/fixtures/qram_read_std_array.cpp:25).

Result: the C1 / H1 / H4 rewrite shapes work end-to-end against fixture stubs (and through test_qram_e2e.cpp), but a user writing the natural syntax in their own .cpp against the real qint_alias.hpp gets a hard parse error from clang.

Scope (single-file production change + small parse test):
- include/sturm/qtypes/qint_alias.hpp: add a templated converting constructor

      template <std::size_t W>
      qint(const ::sturm::qint_t<W>& src) noexcept;

  with definition that mirrors the fixture's "no-op except for the implicit operator size_t() consumer" semantics — the body never executes at runtime in the C1/H1/H4 rewrite path because the plugin REPLACES the VarDecl initializer before codegen. The constructor only needs to make the source PARSE. Forward-declare sturm::qint_t in the header if needed; do NOT pull in the full qint.hpp transitively (would explode include time and risk circular deps).
- New test tests/qtypes/test_qint_alias_qint_t_init.cpp (≤120 LoC):
  - Compile-only check: `qint b = a[i]` parses against the real production header for std::array, C-array, and pointer container shapes.
  - Asserts the converting constructor is constexpr/noexcept (or whichever is most natural).
  - Does NOT exercise runtime semantics; the rewrite path is covered by test_qram_e2e.cpp.
- Update examples/qram_demo.cpp to use the natural transpiler-rewrite syntax (qint b = a[i]; b = a[j]; qint c = a[i] + d;) so it actually demonstrates how an end user writes QRAM code, not the runtime API. The current telemetry-only demo body can become a smaller [secondary] section.

Done when:
- ctest -R "qint_alias_qint_t_init" --parallel 6 green.
- ctest -L qram --parallel 6 still 100% green (no regression in the rewrite end-to-end tests).
- example_qram_demo builds clean and prints the C1/H1/H4 outputs from the natural source.

Threading: every cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocation MUST be capped at -j6 / --parallel 6. NO EXCEPTIONS.

title: B5: end-to-end gate-stream + statevector test (closes v1)
description:
Plan beat B5 — docs/plan_qram_backend.md §5.

Goal: Pin the v1 contract end-to-end with the public QRAM_read(a, i, b) entry-point — not the internal helper — so the test exercises every layer (overload dispatch → mask-OR routing → QROM helper → DSL body → adjoint → split counter).

New test: tests/qram/test_qram_read_qrom_gates.cpp (≤300 LoC)

Fixture: (N, W) = (4, 4) with a = {0xA, 0x5, 0xF, 0x0}.

1. Forward record pin (G5). Install RecordingSink. Call QRAM_read(a, i, b) with classical i = 2. Assert:
   - exact CX count and CCX count match per-k budget computed from (N, W, popcount(a[k]))
   - every record's op ∈ {quantum_xor, quantum_and}
   - one record for qrom_read, zero for qreg_read
   - umbrella qram::qram_read_count() == 1
   - i.super_mask == 0 after the call (PRD §11.2.7 item 3)

2. Round-trip pin (G3). Same fixture. Forward + adjoint leaves b empty: assert via statevector P(b == 0) ≈ 1.0. Assert recorded gate stream is balanced (every primitive appears even times across round trip).

3. Superposed-index pin (G1). With i in (|0⟩+|2⟩)/√2 (H on i.bit(1)), run forward read, assert P(b=a[0]) + P(b=a[2]) ≈ 1.0, each ≈ 0.5; assert i.super_mask unchanged.

4. Out-of-range UB document (PRD §5). Test does NOT call i = 5 on N = 4 — that's UB. Comment in test explains why and refers to PRD §5.

Production: none; only the test lands. All production code already in place from B0–B4.

In this commit: docs/prd_qram_backend.md Status flips from 'Draft' to 'Implemented'.

title: B2: sequential XOR-fanout DSL body (lib_qram_read_qrom_dsl)
B2a: predicate compute/uncompute helper (lib_qram_eq_k)
description:
Plan beat B2a — docs/plan_qram_backend.md §5.

Goal: Factor the predicate-ancilla compute/uncompute step out of the QROM body. New header include/sturm/detail/lib/qram_read_predicate.hpp provides:

  template <std::size_t W>
  inline void lib_qram_eq_k_compute(qint_t<W>& i, std::size_t k, std::size_t K, qbool& eq_k);

  template <std::size_t W>
  inline void lib_qram_eq_k_uncompute(qint_t<W>& i, std::size_t k, std::size_t K, qbool& eq_k);

Compute step bit-flips bits of i whose corresponding bit of k is 0 (using i.bit(j).flip()), AND-reduces the active K bits onto eq_k via lib_c_n_AND_dsl, then bit-flips back. Uncompute is the same body — predicate is self-inverse — provided as a named entry-point so QROM body and adjoint both call by name (placement-audit tooling, P9c spirit).

Helper does NOT modify i net — every flip() is paired — but temporarily perturbs i's value bits during the call. Qubits are unchanged at scope exit.

Files (new):
- include/sturm/detail/lib/qram_read_predicate.hpp (≤200, ~80 LoC expected)

New test: tests/lib/test_qram_read_predicate.cpp (≤250 LoC)

- For superposed i (set super_mask manually), recording-sink pins gate-set: only quantum_xor and quantum_and chain from c_n_AND
- Statevector test: K=2, i in uniform superposition over 4 basis states via OrkanBridge apply_h, run lib_qram_eq_k_compute with k=1 → assert P(eq_k=1) ≈ 0.25, then uncompute and assert P(eq_k=0) ≈ 1.0 (peak qubits: 4)

title: modular-arith: lift kMaxN beyond 32 for circuit-generation use cases

  - Bump STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY in CMakeLists.txt to a chosen target (W=64 needs 512, W=128 needs 1024, W=256 needs 2048; pick based on use case).

Ref: epic sturm-4oot final state (post sturm-4oot.6 audit). Public docs (docs/public_api.md) currently list no W cap; revisit if a cap is documented elsewhere.

title: even-n-double-mod: thread (W-1)-bit lt_flags register through lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot
description:
Update lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot (and __lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot_adj) to allocate a (W-1)-bit 'lt_flags' register and pass one bit per inner doubling.

Forward (mul_mod_dsl_oneshot.hpp step 4b): each lib_double_mod_dsl call gets lt_flags[i] as its lt_flag_out (i = 0..W-2). The lt_flags register lives through the forward+uncompute pass; on the reverse pass (step 6a) each __lib_double_mod_dsl_adj consumes its lt_flags[i] and zeros it. After step 6a's last call lt_flags is uniformly 0; release LIFO.

Add an entry-time precondition that lt_flags enters in |0> (pool allocation guarantees this).

Update layered ancilla bookkeeping in the header preamble: peak goes from ≈ 2W + 8 to ≈ 3W + 7 (add (W-1) for the lt_flags register; subtract 1 since the inner double_mod no longer allocates its own lt_flag). See docs/design_even_n_double_mod.md §8.

title: even-n-double-mod: rewrite lib_double_mod_dsl + adjoint with lt_flag_out
description:
Implement Strategy Y from docs/design_even_n_double_mod.md (sturm-fya1).

Change signature of lib_double_mod_dsl and __lib_double_mod_dsl_adj to take an extra 'Bit& lt_flag_out' parameter. Forward XORs (2x_orig < n_value) into lt_flag_out; adjoint reads lt_flag_out to reverse the doubling and leaves it = 0 on exit.

Drop the LSB-trick uncompute step (forward step 8: 'lt_flag ^= x_bits[0]; lt_flag.flip()'; adjoint step 3': 'lt_flag.flip(); lt_flag ^= x_bits[0]'). The internal lt_flag allocation goes away.

Drop the odd-n precondition from both header doxygen blocks; document the new lt_flag_out contract instead. Note that the SWAP rotation, the conditional add-back via lift_under(lt_flag_own), and the carry_anc cleanup remain unchanged; only the lt_flag bit's lifetime moves out to the caller.

This issue blocks #2..#5 of the sturm-fya1 plan (test extensions, mul_mod_oneshot rewiring, dispatcher removal). See docs/design_even_n_double_mod.md §3 and §8 for the new API and the post-fix interior peak (n_pad + carry_anc + inner adder carry + lift CCX fold = 4).

HARD LIMIT: All cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocations capped at 6 threads (--parallel 6 / -j6). See CLAUDE.md.

title: even-n-double-mod: extend lib_double_mod_dsl to handle even n (plan)
description:
Plan how to lift the odd-n restriction on `lib_double_mod_dsl` (sturm-wdas, Beat B of the O(W) modular-kernels epic sturm-4oot) so the new O(W) modular-multiplication path can run for ANY modulus, not just classically-odd ones.

## Why this matters

Beat B's `lib_double_mod_dsl` requires `n` odd because its `lt_flag`-uncompute step (`lt_flag ^= x[0]; lt_flag.flip();`) exploits the result LSB. For even `n`, the result LSB is always 0 and doesn't encode `lt_flag`, so the cleanup leaves a dirty ancilla that breaks reversibility.

This restriction propagated up to Beat C (sturm-7cix, mul-mod-rewrite). The worker resolved it with a runtime dispatcher: `lib_mul_mod_dsl` now routes to the new O(W) `lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot` when `n` is classically known to be odd, and falls back to the existing O(W^2) chain otherwise. Tests that don't propagate the classical odd-n hint (notably the lib-level tests, which use the 1-arg `qbool::make_non_owning(idx)` factory) keep hitting the slow chain path. Until Beat B is extended, the chain fallback and dispatcher have to stay alive.

## Deliverable

A short design doc (≤ 1 page, in `docs/`) that:

1. **Surveys how reversible modular doubling is handled classically.** What does the published reversible-arithmetic literature say? Häner-Roetteler-Svore "Optimizing Quantum Circuits for Arithmetic" and follow-ups (Roetteler et al. on Shor's algorithm) cover modular arithmetic primitives — does any of them carry an explicit `lt_flag`-uncompute construction that handles even moduli? Are there classical hardware/software reversible-arithmetic libraries (revlib, Quipper's modular kernels) that handle this case? What ancilla cost do they pay?

2. **Picks one of the candidate strategies** (X/Y/Z below, or a new one suggested by the literature):

   - **Strategy X — extra comparison ancilla.** Compute `cmp = (x_old < n/2)` via `compare_dsl` BEFORE the doubling dance, use `cmp` to clean `lt_flag` after the dance (they're equal). Open question: how to clean `cmp` — `__compare_adj` needs `x_old`, which is gone after the in-place dance. Options: (a) keep a W-bit copy of `x_old` alive for the duration (+ W ancillas peak); (b) reconstruct `x_old` from `x_new` via modular halving; (c) some other trick.

   - **Strategy Y — return lt_flag as an output.** Make `lib_double_mod_dsl` a 2-output primitive `(x_new, lt_flag)`. Caller (mul_mod's W-iteration loop) tracks the W `lt_flag` bits as a register and cleans on the reverse pass via adjoint. Adds W ancillas at the mul_mod layer; still O(W) overall.

   - **Strategy Z — a cleverer uncomputation rearrangement.** Beat A's in-place adder cleans `lt_flag` via a 2-extra-adder dance (subtract a, clean, add a) without depending on n's parity. The analog for doubling isn't obvious because the addend (x itself) was overwritten — but maybe a different rearrangement works.

3. **Decides update-in-place vs. sibling primitive.** Either (i) update `lib_double_mod_dsl` in place to handle all n (re-open sturm-wdas, change precondition + tests) or (ii) create a sibling `lib_double_mod_dsl_general` for even n and keep the odd-only fast path. The doc should pick one and justify.

4. **Decides what happens to the dispatcher and chain fallback** in `lib_mul_mod_dsl` once Beat B is general. Likely: dispatcher and chain go away, `kMaxN` lifts further. Spell it out.

5. **Decides Beat D (sturm-3sfl, pow_mod-rewrite) implications.** Beat D's `lib_square_mod_dsl` may have an analogous odd-n issue. Does fixing Beat B cascade up automatically (square = double + something), or does Beat D need its own even-n design? The design doc should note this so Beat D's planner doesn't repeat the analysis.

6. **Decomposes into implementation issues.** A list of follow-up bd issues, each scoped to one piece of the implementation:
   - `even-n-double-mod: implement <chosen strategy> in lib_double_mod_dsl[_general]`
   - `even-n-double-mod: extend tests to all n in [1, 2^W)`
   - `even-n-double-mod: re-pin ancilla budget tests`
   - `even-n-double-mod: drop dispatcher + chain fallback from lib_mul_mod_dsl` (if applicable)
   - `even-n-double-mod: lift kMaxN in mul_mod` (if applicable)

7. **Estimates ancilla budget impact.** Whatever strategy is chosen, the doc should give the new peak-ancilla closed form for `lib_double_mod_dsl` and propagate the impact up to `lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot` and (if applicable) Beat D.

## Out of scope for this planning issue

- Actual implementation. This issue's deliverable is the design doc + decomposed bd issues only.
- Any change to `lib_double_mod_dsl` source (those go in the implementation issues spawned from the plan).

## Hard limits

All cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocations capped at 6 threads (`--parallel 6` / `-j6`). See CLAUDE.md.

## Context links

- sturm-wdas: lib_double_mod_dsl + adjoint (Beat B, landed commit f696c80) — has the odd-n precondition.
- sturm-7cix: mul-mod-rewrite (Beat C, landed commit e8e7d16) — added the dispatcher to work around it.
- sturm-3sfl: pow-mod-rewrite (Beat D, deferred, will likely need this).
- sturm-4oot: o-w-modular-kernels (parent tracking epic).
- `include/sturm/detail/lib/double_mod_dsl.hpp` — Beat B forward.
- `include/sturm/detail/lib/double_mod_dsl_adj.hpp` — Beat B adjoint.
- `include/sturm/detail/lib/mul_mod_dsl.hpp` — current dispatcher.
- `include/sturm/detail/lib/compare_dsl.hpp` — comparison primitive (would be used by Strategy X).
close_reason: Design plan landed at docs/design_even_n_double_mod.md. Decomposed implementation issues filed under epic sturm-4oot (sturm-4oot.1..sturm-4oot.6) with blocking deps wired. Strategy: Y (expose lt_flag as output). Math reason: x → 2x mod n is 2-to-1 for even n, so the bit cannot be absorbed locally. Beat D (sturm-3sfl) inherits the conclusion and flagged in the design doc §6.

title: mul-mod-rewrite: rewrite lib_mul_mod_dsl on in-place primitives (Beat C)
description:
Rewrite lib_mul_mod_dsl (and its __lib_mul_mod_dsl_adj sibling) to use a single accumulator + single shifted register, lowering qubit cost from O(W^2) to O(W).

New algorithm shape:
  shifted_reg: W+1 qubits, initialized to a (top bit = overflow slot)
  acc_reg:     W qubits, initialized to 0

  for i = 0..W-1:
      if b[i]: lib_add_mod_inplace_dsl(shifted_reg, acc_reg, n)   # Beat A
      if i < W-1: lib_double_mod_dsl(shifted_reg, n)              # Beat B

  r ^= acc_reg

  # Uncompute: reverse loop with adjoint primitives
  for i = W-1..0:
      if i < W-1: __lib_double_mod_dsl_adj(shifted_reg, n)
      if b[i]: __lib_add_mod_inplace_dsl_adj(shifted_reg, acc_reg, n)

  # Final: zero shifted_reg, acc_reg → release

Total internal qubits: shifted_reg (W+1) + acc_reg (W) + small ancillas ≈ 3W + O(1).

Replaces the existing chain-style implementation in include/sturm/detail/lib/mul_mod_dsl.hpp:170-208 (shifted_chain[W][W] + r_chain[W][W]).

Public sturm::mul_mod (qint_modular.hpp) signature is unchanged. Existing tests (tests/lib/test_mul_mod_dsl.cpp, test_mul_mod_dsl_adjoint.cpp) must pass unchanged.

Downstream effect: lift kMaxN from 8 in mul_mod_dsl.hpp:160. Pick a new cap consistent with the simulator's 17-qubit ceiling (likely W ≤ 14 with O(W) qubit cost).

Layering: per PRD §4 'no new gate emission'. Built on Beat A + Beat B + lift_under + the existing XOR-copy pattern. No new arithmetic kernel.

HARD LIMIT: All cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocations capped at 6 threads (--parallel 6 / -j6). See CLAUDE.md.
design:
Open design questions for this beat:

1. **kMaxN cap.** Today's cap is 8 because of the O(W^2) qubit budget vs. simulator's 17-qubit ceiling. With O(W), peak qubits ≈ 3W + (Beat A's ~W+5) + (small overhead) ≈ 4W + 10ish. So 17-qubit cap → W ≤ 14 ish, likely set kMaxN=14 or 12 for headroom. Confirm with a live-qubit ancilla counter test.

2. **Existing test compatibility.** sturm::mul_mod public signature unchanged means tests/lib/test_mul_mod_dsl.cpp should run unmodified. But: ancilla-counter tests (if any) will see different numbers — update those expectations as part of this beat. Check tests/lib/CMakeLists.txt for any lib-level tests that assert specific qubit counts.

3. **Adjoint round-trip.** Round-trip test must cover both the forward+adjoint pair AND the W-loop unrolling cleanly zeros all internal registers. Mirror sturm-kubb's adjoint-roundtrip test shape.

4. **Squaring-aliasing case.** Today's lib_mul_mod_dsl docstring (mul_mod_dsl.hpp:138-139) notes 'a_bits and b_bits may alias (the chain-style internal allocation handles the squaring case used by lib_pow_mod_dsl)'. The new in-place design must preserve this behavior — when called with a==b (i.e., compute a^2 mod n), the algorithm must still work because the XOR-copy a→shifted_reg makes a separate physical register, breaking the alias before the loop runs. Confirm with a dedicated squaring test.

5. **Test sub-issue plan.** When claiming, file children mirroring sturm-kubb: n==0 no-op, single classical case, W=2 exhaustive sweep, W=3 random sweep, squaring case, adjoint round-trip, ancilla counter (≤ ~4W+10), pool live-count round-trip, kMaxN-cap lift validation.

title: double-mod-dsl: lib_double_mod_dsl + adjoint (Beat B)
description:
Add lib-level in-place modular doubling primitive plus its sibling adjoint:

  lib_double_mod_dsl(x_bits, n_bits, n, ...)
    x := (2x) mod n

This is NOT lib_add_mod_dsl(x, x, n) — that aliasing case is exactly what's blocked by lib_add_dsl's distinct-qubits rule. Instead, doubling is implemented as a structural shift + conditional-subtract:
  1. Logical left-shift of x by one position. Reversibly, this is a qubit relabeling: append |0> at the bottom (new LSB) and the original top bit becomes the overflow slot at position W. No gates emitted — pointer/view manipulation only.
  2. Conditional subtract n if the result is ≥ n. Reuse the trial-subtract / conditional-add-back idiom from lib_add_mod_dsl steps 6–11.

Crucially, this primitive does NOT call lib_add_dsl with aliased operands at any point — the only adder use is the unconditional subtract of n during reduction, which has distinct (n_extended, x_extended) operands.

Mandatory adjoint sibling __lib_double_mod_dsl_adj computing x := x/2 mod n. Defined when the LSB is 0 — which holds after one full forward call (since (2x) mod n always has LSB derived from the doubled x's bits). Document precondition explicitly.

No public wrapper at this beat — kept private under detail/lib/. Beat C will lower lib_mul_mod_dsl onto this primitive together with Beat A.

Layering: per PRD §4 'no new gate emission'. The shift step is gate-free (relabeling); the reduction reuses the lib_add_dsl / detail_div::lib_add_adj pair from add_mod_dsl.

HARD LIMIT: All cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocations capped at 6 threads (--parallel 6 / -j6). See CLAUDE.md.
design:
Open design questions to resolve before/during implementation:

1. **Shift-as-relabel mechanics.** Need to verify that STURM's qubit-pool / view machinery (qint_t::make_non_owning, BitProxy(qbool&), etc.) supports constructing a 'shifted view' of x_bits that maps logical bit i to physical qubit i-1, plus a |0> ancilla at logical position 0. Reading qint_core / qbool, non-owning views over different qubit indices look routine — but lift_under and WHEN guards must still work correctly through such views. Verify with a small spike before committing to the algorithm.

2. **Top-bit handling.** When x is doubled, the original x[W-1] becomes part of the (W+1)-bit intermediate. After conditional subtract of n, the top bit must end up cleared (otherwise x grows beyond W bits). Confirm the trial-subtract-then-add-back idiom drops the overflow bit cleanly — same shape as lib_add_mod_dsl, so should hold.

3. **Adjoint precondition (LSB == 0).** The forward operation produces x_new whose LSB equals the discarded overflow bit XORed in via the modular reduction; need to verify mathematically that x_new's LSB is in fact 0 unconditionally so the halving adjoint is well-defined. Counterexample search: if x = (n+1)/2 mod n, then 2x mod n = 1 → LSB is 1. So the unconditional-LSB-zero claim is FALSE in general. The adjoint precondition must instead be 'the input was produced by a forward double_mod call with known prior x' OR the adjoint must take auxiliary information. Resolve before implementation — this is the trickiest correctness question in this beat.

   Likely resolution: keep the adjoint paired strictly with its forward call (used only inside Beat C's uncompute pass), where the prior x is known to the caller and reconstruction is via the gate-reverse, not a literal halving operation. Document accordingly.

4. **Test plan.** Mirror sturm-yh3d's children: n==0 no-op, single classical case, W=2 exhaustive sweep, W=3 random sweep, adjoint round-trip, ancilla counter, pool live-count round-trip. Plus one test specifically exercising the (n+1)/2 case from #3. File as children when claiming.

title: add-mod-inplace-dsl: in-place lib_add_mod_inplace_dsl + adjoint (Beat A)
description:
Add lib-level in-place modular addition primitive plus its sibling adjoint:

  lib_add_mod_inplace_dsl(a_bits, dest_bits, n_bits, n, ...)
    dest := (dest + a) mod n

Today's lib_add_mod_dsl is out-of-place — it allocates a fresh (W+1)-bit s register internally, computes (a+b) mod n there, and XOR-copies into r. The in-place variant skips the XOR-copy step and uses dest directly as the carrier. The trial-subtract-then-conditional-add-back idiom (steps 6–11 of add_mod_dsl.hpp's preamble) is unchanged; only the destination plumbing changes.

Mandatory adjoint sibling __lib_add_mod_inplace_dsl_adj computing dest := (dest - a) mod n, in include/sturm/detail/lib/add_mod_inplace_dsl_adj.hpp, mirroring the add_mod_dsl.hpp / add_mod_dsl_adj.hpp pairing pattern.

No public wrapper at this beat — kept private under detail/lib/. Beat C will lower lib_mul_mod_dsl onto this primitive.

Layering: build strictly on lib_add_dsl + detail_div::lib_add_adj + lift_under, per PRD §4 'no new gate emission' rule. No new arithmetic kernel.

HARD LIMIT: All cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocations capped at 6 threads (--parallel 6 / -j6). See CLAUDE.md.
design:
Open design questions to resolve before/during implementation:

1. **Overflow-bit handling.** Today's algorithm computes (a+b) into an internal (W+1)-bit s register so the trial-subtract has room for the overflow bit. If dest *is* the carrier instead of s, dest needs to be W+1 qubits wide so the top bit can act as the overflow slot, OR a different reduction strategy is needed. Probable resolution: caller passes dest as W+1 qubits, top bit acts as the overflow slot. Keeps the algorithm structurally identical to add_mod_dsl. Confirm during implementation.

2. **Ancilla budget.** Target: peak ancilla ≤ W+5 (i.e. lt_flag, n_pad, carry_anc, plus whatever lib_add_dsl needs internally). Add a pool round-trip test and an ancilla counter test, mirroring sturm-yh3d.6 and sturm-yh3d.7.

3. **Aliasing precondition.** a_bits and dest_bits must refer to physically distinct qubits (inherited from lib_add_dsl). Document explicitly in the doxygen and verify with at least one same-pointer-different-qubits test where appropriate.

4. **Test plan symmetry with sturm-yh3d.** Mirror the structure used for the original add_mod: n==0 no-op, single classical case, W=2 exhaustive sweep, W=3 random sweep, adjoint round-trip, ancilla counter, pool live-count round-trip. File these as children when claiming the beat — not up front.

title: o-w-modular-kernels: O(W) modular kernels via in-place primitives (epic)
description:
Collapse the O(W^2) qubit cost in lib_mul_mod_dsl and lib_pow_mod_dsl to O(W) by introducing in-place modular primitives, eliminating the chain-style allocations.

Today's chain workaround exists because lib_add_dsl requires its two operand registers to refer to physically distinct qubits (see maj_dsl in adder_dsl.hpp:71 — the first instruction 'b ^= c' becomes 'q ^= q' if a and b alias the same qubit, destroying the input). Working around this in lib_mul_mod_dsl forces W separate W-bit shifted/r-chain registers; lib_pow_mod_dsl stacks the same workaround, giving ~4W^2 + O(W) peak qubits.

Approach: replace the two chains with single accumulator + single shifted register, driven by two new lib-level primitives:
  - lib_add_mod_inplace_dsl: dest := (dest + a) mod n  (Beat A)
  - lib_double_mod_dsl:       x   := (2x)     mod n   (Beat B, shift-based — sidesteps the aliasing rule entirely)

Then rewrite lib_mul_mod_dsl on top of A+B (Beat C), and optionally apply the same trick one level up for lib_pow_mod_dsl (Beat D).

Public signatures (sturm::add_mod, sturm::mul_mod, sturm::pow_mod) are preserved; existing tests must pass unchanged. Lifting kMaxN=8 in mul_mod is a downstream effect of Beat C.

title: Restore README.md Build section documenting STURM_MODULAR_POW
description:
The full-suite ctest gate trips deterministically on test #59
`cmake_modular_pow_help_text` (label: cmake docs modular-arith). The
test (tests/cmake_modular_pow_help_text.cmake:199-237) reads
README.md, regex-matches a Build anchor of the form `**Build...**`,
`## Build`, or `### Build`, and then requires the slice from that
anchor onward to mention three needles: `STURM_MODULAR_POW`, `OFF`,
`lib_pow_mod_dsl`. README.md currently has no such anchor.

Root cause (NOT introduced by today's autopilot run):
- The test was introduced in commit a30c420 (sturm-bjt2.1, "P6.1
  cmake-flag-help-text"). At that time README.md had a
  `**Build from source (contributors):**` line which satisfied the
  anchor.
- Commit 19cbafb (sturm-8gvh.3, "E8.M3 README.md prereqs +
  install/consume flow") rewrote the README and dropped the bold
  Build heading. The Build-section content moved into
  `## Developer build (working on STURM itself)`, which the test's
  regex does not accept.
- Today's commits (sturm-b5t4 042a009, sturm-824s 2d7b4ce) did not
  touch any of this — `git show HEAD~1:README.md | grep -E '\*\*Build|^## +Build|^### +Build'`
  returns nothing, confirming the failure predates both commits.
- A separate flakiness memory exists for this test under parallel
  load — that pattern is unrelated; this one fails in isolation
  (reproduced with `ctest -R '^cmake_modular_pow_help_text$'`,
  34.5s, same FATAL_ERROR).

Scope:

1. Edit README.md to add a `## Build` (preferred — explicit and
   stable) section. Place it where the build flag content
   logically belongs (e.g., between `## Install & consume` and
   `## Getting started`, or merged into / immediately preceding
   `## Developer build`). Decide based on which placement reads
   best for a user skimming the README; the test does not care
   about position, only that the anchor exists and the three
   needles appear in the slice from that anchor onward.
2. Inside that Build section, document the `STURM_MODULAR_POW`
   build flag — at minimum it must mention:
     - the flag name `STURM_MODULAR_POW`
     - that the default is `OFF`
     - the gated primitive `lib_pow_mod_dsl`
   These are the three literal needles the test greps for; phrase
   them naturally (e.g., "STURM_MODULAR_POW (default OFF) gates
   the lib_pow_mod_dsl primitive — opt in if you need pow_mod
   support").
3. Do NOT relax or otherwise modify
   tests/cmake_modular_pow_help_text.cmake — the contract being
   enforced (Plan §8.1: the flag must be documented under a Build
   section in README.md) is the right contract; this issue
   restores compliance, not the other way around.
4. Sanity-check by re-reading the README end-to-end after the
   edit so the new section flows with the surrounding prose
   (Prerequisites → Install & consume → Build → Getting started
   → How it works → Developer build, or whatever order you choose).

Acceptance:
- `grep -nE '\*\*Build[^*]*\*\*|^## +Build|^### +Build' README.md`
  matches at least one line.
- The slice of README.md from that anchor to EOF mentions
  `STURM_MODULAR_POW`, `OFF`, and `lib_pow_mod_dsl`.
- `ctest -R '^cmake_modular_pow_help_text$' --output-on-failure`
  passes (run from build/, capped at --parallel 6 if you parallelize).
- The sibling test `cmake_modular_pow_help_text_doc` (#62) still
  passes — it currently does, but the README slice change should
  not regress it.
- README.md still reads as a coherent top-level doc (no orphan
  heading, no duplicated content with `## Developer build` unless
  intentional).

Out of scope: rewriting other parts of README.md, touching
docs/getting_started.md, addressing the parallel-load flakiness
memory for #58/#59 (that is a separate, lower-priority concern).

Cap any cmake/ctest/ninja invocations at -j6 / --parallel 6 per
CLAUDE.md.

title: Rewrite docs/getting_started.md user example to drop .value access
description:
docs/getting_started.md is a user-facing tutorial. Its current main.cpp
code block is a verbatim copy of tests/external_consumer/main.cpp, which
uses qint/qbool .value field reads inside the WHEN body and ships an
extern \"C\" sturm_get_thread_context stub. Both are test-only concerns
(speed + avoiding a libsturm link dependency). User-facing docs must
never show .value access — classical/quantum behaviour is handled by the
backend, and users interact via construction, operator=, and
static_cast<int64_t> / static_cast<bool>.

This issue rewrites the user-facing snippets so the public idiom is
the only thing on the documentation surface.

Depends on: sturm-b5t4 (must remove the byte-equality CI gate first;
otherwise the drift check fails the moment we change the doc).

Scope:

1. docs/getting_started.md — rewrite the main.cpp fenced code block to:
     - keep `qint a = 6, b = 5, n = 7;` and `qbool flag = true;` (already
       idiomatic — uses the implicit ctors at qint_core.hpp:80 and
       qbool.hpp:52).
     - replace `int64_t r = a.value;` with
       `int64_t r = static_cast<int64_t>(a);` (uses the explicit
       operator int64_t at qint_core.hpp:97).
     - replace `(a.value + b.value) % n.value` similarly with
       static_cast<int64_t>(...) on each operand. Keep this inside the
       WHEN body so the WHEN demonstration is preserved.
     - DROP the decltype/static_assert ODR-avoidance block and the
       extern \"C\" sturm_get_thread_context stub. Those exist only to
       keep the smoke test linkable without libsturm; they are not
       something a user should learn or copy.
     - Trim the header comment block to a short user-oriented intro
       (the long PRD/D3/E6.M1 references belong in the test file, not
       the tutorial).
2. docs/getting_started.md prose around the example:
     - Replace the line \"Output: the classical \`.value\` of a guarded
       modular update\" with wording that does not mention .value.
     - Replace \"This is the classical \`.value\` of \`(a + b) mod n\`\"
       with \"the classical value of\".
     - Drop or rewrite the paragraph that explains the file is a
       byte-for-byte mirror of tests/external_consumer/main.cpp (no
       longer true after sturm-b5t4).
3. README.md — rewrite the \"Getting started\" snippet so it shows the
   same idiomatic style as the updated getting_started.md (no
   a.value = 1 / b.value = 0; no manual sturm_backend_create lifecycle
   in the headline example). Keep it short — the full walkthrough still
   lives in getting_started.md.
4. Verify the expected output line `external_consumer: r=4` is still
   accurate for the new snippet (a=6, b=5, n=7, flag=true ⇒ (6+5)%7=4).

Acceptance:
- grep -n '\\.value' docs/getting_started.md README.md returns no
  matches against qint/qbool field access. (Mentions in unrelated prose
  are fine if they don't refer to qint/qbool field access.)
- The doc still reads as a runnable walkthrough — a fresh consumer
  could copy the snippet into a new project and have it compile against
  an installed STURM prefix.
- README and getting_started tell the same story end-to-end (no
  contradictory snippets / setup styles).
- tests/external_consumer/main.cpp is untouched.
- examples/or_circuit.cpp and other in-tree .value users are untouched
  (separate scope, not this issue).

Cap any cmake/ctest/ninja you run at -j6 / --parallel 6 per CLAUDE.md.

title: Decouple getting_started.md from external_consumer/main.cpp byte-equality
description:

title: test_plugin_nested: include path missing for sturm/version.hpp in runtime-compile invocations
description:
Surfaced by the bd-autopilot end-of-queue full-suite gate after sturm-jzeb. test_plugin_nested (#32, transpiler) shells out a compile of examples/zero_ancilla_fusion.cpp, which #include <sturm/sturm.hpp> -> <sturm/version.hpp>. The test fixture's compile command does not pass ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/include, so the generated sturm/version.hpp is not found.

This is the same family of bug as sturm-hvzy and sturm-jzeb (which fixed CMake link/INTERFACE wiring for build-time targets). test_plugin_nested is the runtime-compile equivalent: it constructs its own compiler invocation at test time and must be passed the include dir for the generated header.

Failure mode (verbatim):
  /Users/sorenwilkening/Desktop/STURM-C++/include/sturm/sturm.hpp:38:10: fatal error: 'sturm/version.hpp' file not found
     38 | #include <sturm/version.hpp>
        |          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Failed assertions in transpiler/tests/test_plugin_nested.cpp:
  - line 295: file_exists(legacy_obj) — 'legacy rewritten .o not produced'
  - line 313: r.exit_code == 0 — 'plugin nested compile failed'
  - line 315: file_exists(plugin_obj) — 'plugin nested invocation did not produce .o'
  - line 321/322: !legacy_dump.empty() / !plugin_dump.empty()

Investigate transpiler/tests/test_plugin_nested.cpp and the harness/CMake glue that hands the test the compile command (look for where -I flags or CMAKE_BINARY_DIR-derived paths are passed to the legacy and plugin nested compile invocations). Likely fix: thread ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/include into the test's command-line construction (target_compile_definitions in tests/transpiler/CMakeLists.txt, or an analogous mechanism), and/or have sturm-transpile plugin propagate the include dir to its nested frontend action.

Verify by:
  cmake --build build --parallel 6 --target test_plugin_nested
  ctest --test-dir build -R '^test_plugin_nested$' --output-on-failure --parallel 6

Cap every cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocation at 6 parallel threads.
close_reason: Threaded ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/include into test_plugin_nested via new STURM_PLUGIN_GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR define; both the legacy (sturm-transpile -- ...) and clang++ -c invocations now pass -I for the generated header dir so sturm/version.hpp is found. Verified via ctest -R test_plugin_nested (passed in 37s).

test_when_lossy_gate_equiv (red): WHEN(ctrl) { a *= b; } gate-equivalence
description:
RED-bar end-to-end test for the fix in epic sturm-8aq3. Mirrors the LO-0.4 acceptance row in `docs/plan_lossy_compound_reversibility.md:58` (`tests/backend/test_when_lossy_gate_equiv.cpp`) — if a file at that path already exists, extend it; otherwise create it.

Goal: prove that a controlled lossy compound assignment produces the gate-level same effect as the by-hand controlled allocate-compute-CSWAP-uncompute shape under a superposed `ctrl` qubit.

Scope:
- Build two equivalent gate lists for `WHEN(ctrl) { a *= b; }` (and at least one of `a &= b;` or `a |= b;` to cover the single-ancilla family besides multiply):
  1. The transpiler-emitted shape (pulled through the LO-2 desugar; can be the literal post-transpile source from the relevant fixture under `tests/transpiler/fixtures/when_lossy_*.expected.cpp`, or constructed directly by calling `mul_oop(a, b, tmp); swap(a, tmp); ... mul_oop_adj(a, b, tmp); swap(a, tmp);` inside an explicit `WhenGuard(ctrl)`).
  2. The reference shape: same forward op, but with the swap implemented as a per-bit Fredkin `for i: lib_swap_dsl(BitProxy(a,i), BitProxy(b,i))` under the same WhenGuard.
- Run both under a small simulator (`tests/backend` already has the harness — see existing `test_when_*` tests for the pattern), with `ctrl` initialized into `(|0>+|1>)/sqrt(2)` and a small operand register.
- Assert the final state vectors match (or the recorded gate lists match modulo equivalent rewrites — pick whichever `tests/backend/` already does).

This test must FAIL on main (the (1) shape emits zero gates for the swap under control, so the operands branch differently from (2)) and PASS after the swap is made control-aware in epic sturm-8aq3.

title: test_when_swap_qint_unit (red): sturm::swap under fake control stack
description:
RED-bar unit test for the fix in epic sturm-8aq3.

Goal: drive `sturm::swap(qint_t<W>&, qint_t<W>&)` under a manually-pushed control stack at depth==1 and assert the emitted gate sequence is per-bit Fredkin (3-CNOT chain) rather than zero gates.

Scope:
- New file: `tests/qtypes/test_when_swap_qint.cpp` (or co-locate with existing `tests/qtypes/test_*.cpp` style; check the directory's CMakeLists for the test-add macro).
- Build a small (W=2 or W=3) qint_t pair with allocated qubits, install a BackendContext, push one ctrl qubit onto `ctx.control_stack`, call `sturm::swap(a, b)`.
- Assert the recorded gate list contains exactly `3 * W` CCX entries (each bit's Fredkin = 3 CCX under one control), and no plain SWAP / CX. Operand ordering: per-bit `(ctrl, a_i, b_i)` for the first and third Toffoli of each bit pair, `(ctrl, b_i, a_i)` for the middle one — confirm via the existing pattern used by `tests/test_invert.cpp` or the `test_when_*` family.
- Also assert a depth==0 control-of: pop the ctrl, repeat the call on a fresh pair, assert zero gates emitted and `a.qubits[]`/`b.qubits[]` swapped (preserves the existing fast-path contract).
- Per-bit `super_mask` propagation: after the depth==1 call, both `a.super_mask` and `b.super_mask` should have the bits at indices [0, W) set (`BitProxy::ensure_quantum` does `*mask_ptr |= (1<<bit_pos)`).

This test must FAIL before the implementation lands (current swap emits zero gates under control) and PASS after.

Acceptance: `ctest -R when_swap_qint --parallel 6` red on main, green after implementation child closes.

title: LO-2 sturm::swap not control-aware: violates PRD §5.1 (epic)
description:
The LO-2 transpiler emits unqualified `swap(<lhs>, __sturm_tmp_<op>_<N>);` after every lossy compound assignment (`*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `&=`, `|=`). ADL resolves that to `sturm::swap(qint_t<W>&, qint_t<W>&)` defined in `include/sturm/qtypes/lossy_oop.hpp:58-65`. That overload unconditionally swaps `value`, `super_mask`, `qubits[]`, and `owning_` and emits zero gates regardless of whether a `WHEN(ctrl)` is active.

PRD §5.1 (`docs/prd_lossy_compound_reversibility.md:291-302`) specifies that under `WHEN(ctrl)` the swap must become per-bit controlled-SWAP (Fredkin), with the reverse swap and uncompute lifted identically. Today the swap silently relabels qubit indices outside the control's scope, so a controlled lossy compound assignment produces wrong gate-level semantics.

Approach (decision settled): make `sturm::swap(qint_t<W>&, qint_t<W>&)` consult `sturm_get_thread_context()->control_stack.depth()`. Depth 0 keeps the existing classical index-relabel (zero gates). Depth >= 1 runs a per-bit `lib_swap_dsl` loop over `BitProxy(a, i)`/`BitProxy(b, i)`. `BitProxy::operator^=` -> `ensure_quantum()` already updates `super_mask` per bit, so the 3-CNOT Fredkin chain inside `lib_swap_dsl` propagates per-bit superposition state correctly without manual bookkeeping. `value`/`owning_` are NOT swapped on the controlled branch (cannot hold a single classical truth on a superposed swap; gate state is the truth).

Edit point only: `include/sturm/qtypes/lossy_oop.hpp:58-65`. No transpiler-text change. No new `STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT` (Fredkin self-inverse). The reverse swap in the LO-2 scope-exit cleanup picks up the new behavior automatically.

Children file the red tests first (gate-equivalence + unit), then the implementation, then the regression sweep.

title: Bug: build_example_user_routine fails — PM3-3 fires on apply_rotation callsite
description:
Surfaced by the Phase N autopilot final-suite run (2026-04-23). Three ctest targets fail at build time:
  - build_example_user_routine (Failed)
  - transpiler_example_user_routine_injected (Not Run — dep failed)
  - transpiler_idempotent_example_user_routine (Not Run — dep failed)

Error: examples/user_routine.cpp:210:9: error: STURM: call to 'apply_rotation' requires uncomputation (has quantum output parameter), but no adjoint is registered. Use STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT(apply_rotation, <adjoint_fn>) at TU scope.

Root cause (apparent): PM3-3 "missing adjoint" diagnostic (transpiler/src/matcher_user_routine.cpp:283, via DiagContext::report_missing_adjoint) fires on the unregistered callee apply_rotation which has a quantum output parameter (qbool& out). examples/user_routine.cpp:155 only registers STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT(rotate_by_k, rotate_by_k_adj) — apply_rotation has no adjoint.

Per the prose at the top of user_routine.cpp, the Case-2 callsite apply_rotation(escape, a) is supposed to be the escaping-output path: PI-3 classifies escape as Final and PI-4 emits no inverse. Either (a) PM3-3 needs an exception for callsites whose quantum outputs are all PI-3-Final-classified, OR (b) apply_rotation needs an explicit STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT (with rotate_by_k_adj delegating, or similar), OR (c) the prose / test expectation is out of date.

user_routine.cpp is unchanged since Phase K PK-5 (4cb3385). Not a Phase-N regression (no rotation/QIR code is touched during this compile path; apply_rotation uses qbool only). Most likely pre-existing, surfaced now because the plugin changed and invalidated the .o cache.

Repro: cmake --build build --parallel 6 --target example_user_routine

Decide approach: PI/PM3 exception vs. registering the adjoint vs. updating the example. Flag B9 P9 compliance before closing.

title: PM1-4 — Nested CompilerInvocation + EmitObjAction

Inside SturmPluginAction::ExecuteAction():

1. Let the parent ASTConsumer (our TranspileConsumer) finish the AST walk and matchAST. QUnit unit_ is populated.
2. Call emit_to_string(unit_, ctx) (from PM1-2) → rewritten string.
3. Clone the current invocation: auto inv = std::make_shared<CompilerInvocation>(getCompilerInstance().getInvocation()); — inherits -O, -I, -D, -std, -flto, -fsanitize, target triple etc. for free.
4. Build an InMemoryFileSystem and addFile(getCurrentFile(), /*mtime*/ 0, llvm::MemoryBuffer::getMemBufferCopy(rewritten)). Overlay on top of real VFS so headers still resolve.
5. Construct child CompilerInstance with cloned invocation + overlay FS. Attach a fresh DiagnosticsEngine backed by the parent's consumer.
6. Execute EmitObjAction (or EmitBCAction / EmitLLVMOnlyAction depending on inv->getFrontendOpts().ProgramAction — inherit the parent's program action so -S, -emit-llvm, -c all work).

If -fplugin-arg-sturm-transpile-dump-to=<path> was passed (PM1-3), write rewritten to that path via io::write_file before the nested invocation.

title: PK-harness-whencapture: WHEN stub in test_matcher_harness.cpp models pre-PK-3 3-if expansion
description:
transpiler/tests/test_matcher_harness.cpp defines kQBoolWhenStub (lines 65-97) — a string containing a stand-in for the WHEN macro used when the matcher is exercised against a synthetic qbool. The stub's macro expansion is a **three-if tower**:

    #define WHEN(expr) \
        if (::sturm::detail::WhenCapture _when_capture_{}; true) \     // outer
        if (decltype(auto) _when_val_ = ...; true) \                    // middle
        if (auto& _when_guard_ = ...; _when_guard_.should_run())         // inner

But the real WHEN macro in include/sturm/control/when.hpp:225-228 is now a **two-if tower**:

    #define WHEN(expr) \
        if (decltype(auto) _when_val_ = ::sturm::detail::materialize_when(expr); true) \
        if (auto _when_guard_ = ::sturm::detail::make_when_guard(_when_val_); \
            _when_guard_.should_run())

The Phase K PK-3 (sturm-pzye) retirement of the WhenCapture layer eliminated the outer if from the real macro. The stub still emits it, along with a placeholder 'struct WhenCapture' definition that no longer exists in the real tree. This means:

- Any matcher whose selection logic anchors on the three-if shape (the comment at line 57-64 explicitly says 'the PF-2 matcher anchors on the middle if in the three-if tower') may be testing an obsolete parent-chain structure.
- If the matcher genuinely doesn't care about the outer if, the stub is still reachable-but-misleading; if the matcher DOES implicitly depend on the three-if structure, there is a latent coverage gap that will only surface when the PF-2 matcher is next modified.

Scope of this issue:
1. Verify whether any live matcher in transpiler/src (particularly matcher_when_lift.cpp / matcher_when_nested.cpp) keys off the three-if shape explicitly (ParentMap walks, CompoundStmt ancestor checks, etc.).
2. Update kQBoolWhenStub to match the two-if expansion used by the real macro.
3. Delete the in-stub 'struct WhenCapture' placeholder and the outer 'if (WhenCapture _when_capture_{}; true)' line.
4. Run ctest -L transpiler to confirm the WHEN-related tests still pass; if any fail, the failure signals a pre-existing coverage gap that PK-harness-whencapture revealed.

Acceptance: stub shape matches include/sturm/control/when.hpp:225-228 verbatim (modulo the test's substitute materialize_when / make_when_guard bodies); test_matcher_harness.cpp has no 'WhenCapture' identifier anywhere; transpiler test suite green.

   - Expectation: at least 1 occurrence of `uncompute_eq_qint(c_eq, a, b)`
   - Actual: 0
   - Source: examples/comparison.cpp

What is NOT the cause
---------------------
- `git diff 89fafc2..f85c1f6 -- transpiler/ examples/ tests/transpiler/` is empty — neither the PL-7 Docker work nor the PL-6 preflight touched any of the transpiler, example, or check-script code these tests exercise.
- The PL-3 smoke-fixture fix (tests/smoke/minimal_or.cpp) is in a sibling directory not exercised by these ctest targets.

Likely cause
------------
The autopilot bd memory (bd memories bd-autopilot-agents) notes: "Running the full suite under STURM_AUTO_UNCOMPUTE=OFF surfaces 8 pre-existing unrelated failures." These 3 are a subset. Phase K PK-5 (commit 5b1662a) deleted the STURM_AUTO_UNCOMPUTE flag entirely; before that, AUTO_UNCOMPUTE=ON let the runtime RAII path satisfy the expected-uncompute-call textual grep. After Phase K, the transpile path is the only path — so these three example fixtures and/or their check scripts need updating to match the transpile-only contract (e.g. the qint_arith example may need a `(void)t;` reader to defeat PJ-4a dead-ancilla elim, same as tests/smoke/minimal_or.cpp needed).

Acceptance
----------
- `cmake --build build-release && cd build-release && ctest --output-on-failure` exits 0 on a fresh clone — OR the three tests are deliberately marked WILL_FAIL / DISABLED with a comment citing this bd issue.
- No regression in the 212 tests currently passing.
notes: Root cause: libTooling's Clang driver could not locate its builtin-headers resource directory on macOS, so the parser aborted on 'stdarg.h not found' before main-file translation completed — the three failing examples then produced pass-through output with no uncompute injections. Fixed by baking LLVM_INSTALL_PREFIX/lib/clang/LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR into sturm-transpile at compile time via STURM_CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR, and injecting it via ArgumentsAdjuster(BEGIN) in main.cpp. All 215 tests pass. The issue's PJ-4a (void)t; hypothesis was wrong — the real cause was parse-failure-induced AST truncation.

title: Phase L PL-4: packaging/homebrew/sturm-transpile.rb formula against v0.1.0 tarball
description:

End-user flow (once PL-6 lands)
-------------------------------
