  brew install sturm-transpile

Formula content
---------------
Path: packaging/homebrew/sturm-transpile.rb

```ruby
class SturmTranspile < Formula
  desc "C++ DSL transpiler for quantum-classical programming with compile-time uncompute"
  homepage "https://github.com/SoerenWilkening/Sturm_CPP"
  url "https://github.com/SoerenWilkening/Sturm_CPP/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.0.tar.gz"
  sha256 "PLACEHOLDER_FILLED_AT_PL6"
  license "AGPL-3.0-or-later"

  depends_on "cmake" => :build
  depends_on "llvm@17"

  def install
    llvm = Formula["llvm@17"]
    system "cmake", "-B", "build", "-S", ".",
           "-DLLVM_DIR=#{llvm.opt_lib}/cmake/llvm",
           "-DClang_DIR=#{llvm.opt_lib}/cmake/clang",
           "-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release",
           *std_cmake_args
    system "cmake", "--build", "build"
    system "cmake", "--install", "build"
  end

  test do
    (testpath/"src.cpp").write <<~CPP
      #include <sturm/sturm.hpp>
      void f() { qbool a{0}, b{0}; qbool tmp = a | b; (void)tmp; }
    CPP
    system "#{bin}/sturm-transpile", "src.cpp", "--output-dir", testpath/"out",
           "--extra-arg=-I#{include}", "--extra-arg=-std=c++20"
    assert_match "uncompute_or", (testpath/"out/src.cpp").read
  end
end
```

Note: sha256 stays as PLACEHOLDER in this issue. PL-6 fills it from the actual v0.1.0 source tarball's SHA256SUMS entry.

title: Phase L PL-3: smoke-test matrix prebuilt binary on clean VM without system LLVM
description:
Regression guard that the prebuilt binary from PL-2 runs on a target platform with NO system LLVM installed — catches RPATH misconfiguration, missing bundled dylibs, and cl::opt double-registration regressions (the bug transpiler/CMakeLists.txt:84 already dodges, but which can resurface under different link orders).

Integration point
-----------------
New `smoke-test` job in .github/workflows/release.yml, depending on the build matrix. Reuses the same 4-platform matrix. Runs AFTER each build job produces its artifact but BEFORE the release asset upload step — so a smoke-test failure aborts the release on that platform.

Per-platform smoke-test job
---------------------------
1. Fresh hosted runner (no LLVM install step — verify clean state by asserting `which clang-17` returns non-zero or `apt list --installed 2>/dev/null | grep -c llvm-17-dev` == 0 on Linux).
2. Download the build job's tarball artifact via `actions/download-artifact`.
3. Extract: `tar xzf sturm-transpile-*-$TRIPLE.tar.gz`.
4. Assert `bin/sturm-transpile --help` returns exit 0 and non-empty stdout.
5. Run transpile: `bin/sturm-transpile tests/smoke/minimal_or.cpp --output-dir /tmp/out --extra-arg=-I$PWD/include/sturm --extra-arg=-std=c++20`.
6. Verify `/tmp/out/minimal_or.cpp` exists AND contains `uncompute_or(`.
7. Optional compile: `clang++ -std=c++20 -I$PWD/include /tmp/out/minimal_or.cpp -c -o /tmp/minimal_or.o` using the system clang (NOT llvm-17 — a different clang, to prove the tool has no hidden LLVM-version lock at runtime).

New fixture
-----------
tests/smoke/minimal_or.cpp — a trivial qbool-OR shape similar to examples/or_circuit.cpp but dependency-free (no tests/ conveniences). Shape:

    #include <sturm/sturm.hpp>
    void f() {
      qbool a{0}, b{0};
      qbool tmp = a | b;
      (void)tmp;
    }

(The `(void)tmp;` reader is deliberate — avoids tripping PJ-4 dead-ancilla elimination; see sturm-3dpf for the legacy or_single_runtime.cpp pattern.)

Acceptance
----------
- release.yml contains 4 build jobs + 4 smoke-test jobs (one smoke-test per build, matrix axis preserved).
- On each of the 4 platforms, smoke-test passes on a fresh runner with no system LLVM.
- Any regression in RPATH / dylib bundling / cl::opt double-registration surfaces as a failing smoke-test with an explicit error message (grep for "registered more than once" in stderr; fail with an explicit message if hit).
- Build jobs pass but smoke-test fails cleanly if the tarball is malformed (e.g. missing lib/ directory).

Depends on: PL-2. Blocks: PL-6.

title: Phase L PL-2: .github/workflows/release.yml tag-triggered 4-platform build
description:
Tag-triggered GitHub Actions workflow producing prebuilt relocatable tarballs for 4 platforms on every v* release. Depends on PL-1 (install rules + versioning).

Trigger: `on: push: tags: 'v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*'`.

Matrix
------

  aarch64-linux   runs-on ubuntu-24.04-arm
  x86_64-macos    runs-on macos-13
  aarch64-macos   runs-on macos-14

Per-platform job steps
----------------------
1. Checkout at tagged commit (`fetch-depth: 0`).
2. Install LLVM 17:
   - Linux: `sudo apt-get install -y llvm-17-dev libclang-17-dev clang-17 cmake patchelf`.
   - macOS: `brew install llvm@17 cmake` (Homebrew already provides install_name_tool).
3. Configure with `cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$PWD/staging/sturm-transpile-$VERSION-$TRIPLE -DLLVM_DIR=... -DClang_DIR=...`.

5. Copy bundled shared libs into staging lib/:
   - Linux: `cp $(dirname $(readlink -f $(which clang-17)))/../lib/libclang-cpp.so.17 libLLVM-17.so staging/.../lib/`.
   - macOS: `cp $(brew --prefix llvm@17)/lib/libclang-cpp.dylib libLLVM.dylib staging/.../lib/`.
6. Patch RPATH to resolve bundled libs via relative path:
   - Linux: `patchelf --set-rpath '$ORIGIN/../lib' staging/.../bin/sturm-transpile`.
   - macOS: `install_name_tool -add_rpath '@loader_path/../lib' staging/.../bin/sturm-transpile` + `install_name_tool -change <abs-path> '@rpath/<libname>' ...` for each bundled dylib's install_name.
7. Include LICENSE + README.md in staging tree root.
8. `tar czf sturm-transpile-$VERSION-$TRIPLE.tar.gz -C staging sturm-transpile-$VERSION-$TRIPLE/`.
9. Compute SHA256 → append to SHA256SUMS.
10. Upload artifact (for PL-3 smoke-test consumption) + upload to GitHub Release (create release if missing; idempotent on retry).

Release assets per v0.1.0
-------------------------

  sturm-transpile-v0.1.0-aarch64-linux.tar.gz

title: Phase K follow-up PK-8: retire or port 15 legacy backend tests to transpile path
description:
Phase K autopilot run (2026-04-17, commits 9d8caa3..3496c81) left 15 backend tests failing in the full suite. Transpiler path is 131/131 green; these are all runtime-uncompute-contract tests whose assertions were written against the pre-Phase-K behavior.

Root cause summary:
- PK-1 flipped STURM_AUTO_UNCOMPUTE default to OFF.
- PK-2 retired lazy_expr materialization (operator| / operator& / operator^ no longer fuse at runtime; fusion is now transpiler-only via PJ-1 ccnot_inplace).
- PK-3 removed destructor-emitted gates (principle B10 — destructors release qubit indices to the pool but do not emit inverses).

These 15 tests assumed the removed behaviors. None were enumerated in any Phase K issue's retire list (PK-4 only named tests/backend/test_uncompute_or.cpp and tests/test_destructor_gate.cpp).

Failing tests + assertion category:

Gate-count pin changed (runtime lazy fusion gone):
- 57 test_qbool_ops::test_qbool_and_expr_xor — asserts gate_count == 1u for c ^= (a&b); now 2 gates
- 50 test_end_to_end::test_count_only_quantum — asserts pinned count == 16

Label registry / required-test audit:
- 51 test_ci_hook::test_backend_label_lists_all_modules — lists retired test names (test_uncompute_op/run/add_const/each_op/or/when_compound_uncompute/promotion/destructor_gate_on/off)

Ancilla-state / roundtrip (destructor no longer emits inverse):
- 43 test_uncompute_qint_compare::test_uncompute_eq_qint_roundtrip
- 60 test_logic_dsl::test_c_and_dsl_ancilla_clean
- 64 test_mul_dsl::test_mul_dsl_truth_table
- 65 test_div_dsl
- 66 test_compare_dsl_truth_tables
- 67 test_mod_dsl_truth_table
- 58 test_adder_dsl
- 59 test_adder_dsl_template
- 72 test_qint_compare_simulate
- 77 test_e2e_pow_mod
- 78 test_e2e_when_nested
- 95 test_m7_template_dsl

Recommended resolution (mirror PK-4's pattern):
1. For each failing test, decide: (a) port assertions to verify the transpile-path gate stream instead of runtime destructor behavior, (b) delete individual sub-tests that pin legacy RAII behavior (analogous to the AC8 deletion in PK-4), or (c) delete whole test files that are pure legacy-RAII regressions with no transpile analogue.
2. Update tests/backend/test_ci_hook.cpp's required-modules list to reflect the current backend test surface (remove the retired names PK-3 deleted).
3. Re-baseline or remove the pinned gate_count in test_end_to_end.cpp and test_qbool_ops.cpp — in the new contract, runtime gate counts for lazy-expression patterns are not contractually fixed; only the transpile-path (gate_equivalence_*) pairs are.

Verification: cmake --build build && ctest --output-on-failure — full suite must be green.

Relates to the Phase K epic (sturm-e7t8, sturm-0x0s, sturm-pzye, sturm-l6jq, sturm-j22a, sturm-jbpo, sturm-nnzb, all closed 2026-04-17).

title: Phase K PK-7: update docs/01_principles.md (B1b, B9, new B10)
description:
Phase K roadmap item 6. Final sub-phase: record the retirement in the principle file. In-place text edits, no renumbering (existing B1..B9 citations preserved).

Changes to docs/01_principles.md:

B1b (line 47) — remove 'may be added later as opt-in mechanisms'. New text:
'Macro-based or AST-based auto-generation is the default: the transpiler pass at compile time registers inverse operations for every construct. Runtime auto-inversion has been retired.'

B9 (line 68) — rewording. New text:
'Two optimization layers in the default runtime path (inlined dispatch, classicality specialization) and one global optimization pass at transpile time. The C++ compiler inlines dispatch logic and constant-folds branches; classicality specialization optimizes the primitive stream at dispatch time; the transpiler performs whole-function rewrites (PJ-1 fusion, PJ-3 hoisting, PJ-4 dead-ancilla elimination).'

New B10 (append after B9):
'B10. Uncomputation is a compile-time concern, not a runtime concern. Inverses are emitted by the transpiler as explicit uncompute_* / ccnot_inplace / invert(routine)(...) calls in the generated source file. Destructors release qubit indices to the pool; they do not emit gates. Ancilla scope (B6) still uses C++ RAII, but scope exit and uncomputation are now separate concerns.'

Also update the 'Principle Check' section at the bottom of docs/roadmap_transpiler_post_mvp.md to reflect that the predicted B1b/B9 revisions have landed.

Verification:
- grep -r 'principle B9\|principle B1b\|B5\|B6' include/ src/ transpiler/ — no existing citation is contradicted by reworded principles.
- Principle numbering stable (no renumber sweep needed).

2. routine_single_out_escapes — output is a function parameter (escapes); expected output is unchanged source (no injection, no diagnostic).
3. routine_inside_when — call inside WHEN(c) { ... } body with local out; inverse lands inside the WHEN body (Phase F insert_before_override).
4. routine_inside_loop — call inside a for-body with local-to-body out; inverse inside the body (Phase H-style).
5. routine_outer_var_reject — call inside a loop body mutating a qint declared above the loop; PH-3-style skip_uncompute=true + stderr diagnostic; no inverse injected.
6. routine_self_adjoint — user registers STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT(my_swap, my_swap); inverse emission is a second call to the same function (tests self-adjoint pairing).

title: Phase I PI-3: output-param liveness/ownership classification
description:
Phase I subphase 3 of 8. Implement the compute-vs-final classification that the user asked for: full liveness analysis, no explicit COMPUTE/FINAL markers. For each output argument of a routine call, walk the AST to classify the underlying VarDecl as Intermediate / IntermediateOuter / Final / SkipWithDiagnostic.

Rules:
- VarDecl declared in the call's enclosing scope or a descendant of it -> Intermediate (uncompute at scope exit).
- VarDecl declared in an ancestor scope still inside the function -> IntermediateOuter (uncompute at the declaring scope's close brace; override insert_before_override).
- Function parameter or namespace/file scope -> Final (NO uncompute, NO diagnostic — escaping value, user's final computation).
- VarDecl declared outside a loop/branch/WHEN body but mutated inside one -> SkipWithDiagnostic (reverse-loop hazard, mirror PH-3 behavior: skip_uncompute=true + stderr diagnostic).

When a single call has multiple outputs with mixed classes, fall back to the most conservative: if any is SkipWithDiagnostic -> skip; else if any is Final -> skip (cannot partially invert a multi-output routine); else uncompute.

Extract the parent-chain walk into a new shared helper classify_output(vd, call, call_scope, ctx, sm, lang) -> OutputClass in transpiler/src/matcher_common.hpp. Refactor matcher_outer_var_guard.cpp (PH-3) to call it — existing PH-3 snapshots must stay byte-identical.

Deliverables:
- New classify_output helper in matcher_common.hpp.
- matcher_user_routine.cpp uses classify_output to drive uncompute placement.
- Optional: PH-3 refactor to share the helper.
- Unit tests covering all four classifications.

Depends on PI-2 (needs routine-call match sites to classify).
acceptance_criteria: classify_output returns correct class for each of the four cases; multi-output conservative-skip rule applied; PH-3 snapshots remain byte-identical; new unit tests pass

title: Phase H PH-3: matcher_outer_var_guard.cpp — diagnostic for outer-scoped mutation in loop/branch/WHEN
description:
Mutating an outer-scoped qint/qbool inside a loop/branch/WHEN body would require reverse-loop synthesis (contradicts P9) to uncompute correctly. Phase H rejects this with a clear diagnostic and skips uncompute for the flagged op rather than producing semantically-wrong output.

New TU transpiler/src/matcher_outer_var_guard.cpp matches XOR_ASSIGN, *_ASSIGN_CONST, *_ASSIGN_QINT kinds. For each match, walks parents: if any ForStmt/WhileStmt/IfStmt/WHEN-expanded-IfStmt is encountered before reaching the result's decl_loc's enclosing CompoundStmt, the mutation is outer. Detect WHEN via is_expansion_of_macro (transpiler/src/matcher_common.hpp:107-125).

On match: fprintf(stderr, '<file>:<line>:<col>: error: STURM: qbool/qint \'<name>\' (declared at <decl line>) is modified inside a for/while/if/WHEN body — automatic uncomputation would require reverse-loop synthesis. Provide a manual adjoint (P9) or restructure.'). Flag QOperation with new bool skip_uncompute=false field (add to transpiler/include/sturm/transpile/qir.hpp QOperation struct). transpiler/src/uncompute_pass.cpp render_uncompute skips ops with skip_uncompute=true. transpiler/src/qir.cpp dump() renders ' [skip_uncompute]' suffix for visibility.

Per-op flag, not per-scope: a scope can contain both 'intermediate, uncompute normally' and 'outer mutation, skipped' ops.

Depends on PH-1 (needs enclosing_scope to identify the enclosing for/while/if/WHEN Stmt).

See docs/implementation_plan_transpiler_phase_h.md #PH-3 for full details.

Schedules two raw_insertions per match: '{' at body->getBeginLoc() and '}' at Lexer::getLocForEndOfToken(body->getEndLoc(), 0, sm, lang). title: Phase H PH-1: scope-finder refactor (enclosing_scope with CompoundStmt/BracelessBody kind)
description:
Phase H requires matchers to see quantum ops inside for/while/if/else bodies — including braceless ones. Today transpiler/src/matcher_common.hpp:54-77 enclosing_compound_stmt walks up parents until a CompoundStmt, returns nullptr otherwise. Every matcher has 'if (!cs) return;' so braceless bodies are silently rejected.

Replace with enclosing_scope(node, ctx) returning {scope_anchor_stmt, kind} where kind is CompoundStmt or BracelessBody. BracelessBody case synthesizes a QScope keyed on the body Stmt's begin loc, with open_brace=body->getBeginLoc() and close_brace=Lexer::getLocForEndOfToken(body->getEndLoc(), 0, sm, lang). All Phase A-G matchers switch to the new API. Braced-body behavior is unchanged — every pre-existing fixture stays byte-identical.

See docs/implementation_plan_transpiler_phase_h.md #PH-1 for full details.

title: Phase G PG-4: simplify WhenGuard — retire AND-fold
description:
Retire the runtime AND-fold in WhenGuard by deleting the ancilla allocation + CCX emission code. Keep the control_stack pop/push swap that maintains the depth-1 invariant.

**Why**: After Phase G's transpiler lowering (PG-1..PG-3) lands, the runtime never sees a nested WHEN whose inner expr needs an AND gate computed at entry — the transpiler has already written the explicit qbool __stu_ctrl = outer & inner; + uncompute_and(...). title: Phase G PG-3: uncompute_and scheduling + pairwise cascade
description:
Close out the matcher emission by scheduling the post-inner-body uncompute_and call. Pairwise cascade for depth ≥ 3 falls out automatically — each (outer, inner) pair fires independently.

**Why**: Without this step the transpiler emits the AND temp but never uncomputes it, leaking a qubit at scope exit. Pairwise cascade is pinned by user decision #2.

**Files**:
- transpiler/src/matcher_when_nested.cpp

**Acceptance criteria**:

title: Multi-matcher scope.ops loses source order — LIFO emission incorrect
description:
When multiple Phase A matchers contribute ops to the same QScope, scope.ops accumulates in matcher-registration / firing order, not source order. As a result, M8's reverse iteration produces the wrong LIFO sequence.

Repro: examples/or_circuit.cpp post-Phase-A. Forward source order is OR (line ~88), NOT (line ~96), XOR_ASSIGN (line ~105). Expected LIFO inverse at the close brace: XOR_ASSIGN, NOT, OR. Actual emitted order: NOT, OR, XOR_ASSIGN. Verified by indentation analysis of build/sturm_gen/examples/or_circuit.cpp (the first-inserted line absorbs the original 4-space indent before '}', yielding 8-space prefix; the subsequent prepended inserts have 4 spaces).

Likely cause: clang::ast_matchers::MatchFinder fires per-matcher passes in some order independent of source order. The OrCallback / NotCallback / XorAssignCallback each append to scope.ops as they fire; without a stable source-order sort, the resulting list reflects matcher pass order, not statement order.

Suggested fix: in transpiler/src/uncompute_pass.cpp::synthesize(), sort each scope.ops by stmt_range.getBegin().getRawEncoding() ascending before iterating in reverse. This pins LIFO to source order regardless of which matcher fired when. Snapshot fixtures each have a single op per scope so they trivially pass either way; the fix is invariant for them. Add a unit test to test_uncompute_pass.cpp that builds a multi-kind scope.ops out of source order and asserts LIFO is recovered.
acceptance_criteria: Add a multi-op multi-kind unit test to test_uncompute_pass.cpp that seeds scope.ops out of source order and asserts the reversed insertions are in source-LIFO order. Verify build/sturm_gen/examples/or_circuit.cpp emits the inverses in true LIFO (XOR_ASSIGN, NOT, OR) for the demo. Full 'transpiler' label still green.
close_reason: Added std::sort by stmt_range.getBegin() ascending in synthesize() so reverse iteration produces true source-LIFO regardless of matcher firing order. Added test_multi_kind_out_of_order_sorted_by_source() that seeds scope.ops in matcher order (NOT, OR, XOR_ASSIGN) and asserts emission order is (XOR_ASSIGN, NOT, OR). Verified build/sturm_gen/examples/or_circuit.cpp lines 111-113 now emit d ^= c; / nc = ~nc; / uncompute_or(c, a, b) in that order. Full transpiler label green except one pre-existing failure (filed as sturm-sfr) orphan to this fix.

KEY FINDINGS FOR LP4 PATTERN DESIGN
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1. PRD SKETCH IS OFF — no cxxConstructExpr on the lazy path.
   The PRD (prd_transpiler_matcher_lazy_peel.md, "Architecture" section) and
   the implementation plan (LP4 "Proposed pattern") both sketch the lazy chain as:
       hasInitializer(ignoringImplicit(cxxConstructExpr(hasArgument(0, ...))))
   but Clang does NOT emit a CXXConstructExpr here. The VarDecl initializer
   flows directly as:
       VarDecl → ExprWithCleanups → ImplicitCastExpr<UserDefinedConversion>
              → CXXMemberCallExpr (the operator qbool() call)
              → [implicit object] ImplicitCastExpr<NoOp>
              → MaterializeTemporaryExpr
              → CXXOperatorCallExpr '|'
   LP4 MUST drop the cxxConstructExpr layer. The correct matcher for the
   lazy branch is approximately:
       auto lazy_init = ignoringImplicit(
           cxxMemberCallExpr(on(ignoringImplicit(or_call))));
   (ignoringImplicit peels ExprWithCleanups and ImplicitCastExpr; Clang's
   matcher traversal treats UserDefinedConversion casts as implicit.)

2. MaterializeTemporaryExpr sits INLINE between the NoOp ImplicitCastExpr
   and the CXXOperatorCallExpr (confirmed — answers PRD question directly).
   ignoringImplicit in Clang 17 does peel MaterializeTemporaryExpr
   (it is an implicit node by ignoresImpCasts/ignoreImplicit semantics,
   tracked under the TraverseMaterializeTemporaryExpr branch of
   IgnoreImplicit). If a future refactor needs to be defensive against
   older Clangs, use materializeTemporaryExpr(has(...)) explicitly —
   but that is not required on 17. Risk R2 in the plan is RETIRED.

3. The user-defined conversion is NOT folded into a single ImplicitCastExpr.
   It is expressed as BOTH:
     (a) ImplicitCastExpr with CastKind <UserDefinedConversion>  AND
     (b) a CXXMemberCallExpr inside it (the actual call to
         OrExpr<qbool>::operator qbool()).
   Matchers can thus bind on either. Using cxxMemberCallExpr(on(...))
   is preferred because it yields the implicit-object subtree directly,
   which is the CXXOperatorCallExpr we want to peel.

4. The MemberExpr's member-name SHOULD NOT be matched by name.
   clang-matchers print it as ".operator qbool" but that string is
   synthesized and fragile. Match by callee().asFunction() or by
   membership in CXXConversionDecl rather than by the spelled name.
   Simpler: don't constrain the member at all — the fact that it is
   a CXXMemberCallExpr whose 'on' side resolves to the '|' CXXOperatorCallExpr
   is already specific enough given the outer VarDecl/type constraints.

5. Implicit casts wrapping the inner CXXOperatorCallExpr are limited to:
     - MaterializeTemporaryExpr (lazy only)
     - ImplicitCastExpr <NoOp> lvalue-to-const-lvalue (lazy only)
   Operands inside the operator call are wrapped with ImplicitCastExpr <NoOp>
   (lvalue-to-const-lvalue on the DeclRefExprs) on BOTH paths. The MVP
   matcher currently passes without explicit ignoringImplicit on the args
   because Clang's hasArgument matcher traversal already ignores parens
   and implicit conversions during binding lookup (verified: MVP's
   snapshot_or_single is green). LP4 should still wrap declRefExpr()
   bindings in ignoringImplicit() defensively, because the shared
   `or_call` matcher is now consumed as a subtree of a larger pattern
   and the implicit contexts may differ.

6. anyOf mutual exclusion holds by construction.
   Eager returns qbool; lazy returns OrExpr<qbool>. A single overload
   resolution cannot produce both; only one of the anyOf branches can
   fire per VarDecl. The debug-build duplicate-match assert proposed
   as R3 mitigation remains cheap insurance but is not critical.

7. Hermetic mock fidelity CONFIRMED.
   /tmp/ast_probe_real_shape.cpp (which adds noexcept, deleted copy/assign,
   and template-<>-specialization-provided conversion body) produces the
   exact same call-site subtree as /tmp/ast_probe.cpp (the LP3 minimal
   mock). Therefore the LP3 hermetic fixture is SAFE — Risk R1 retires
   at LP3+LP4, only to be re-checked at LP5 on the real example.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
RECOMMENDED LP4 PATTERN (REVISED FROM PLAN)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

using namespace clang::ast_matchers;

auto or_call = cxxOperatorCallExpr(
    hasOverloadedOperatorName("|"),
    argumentCountIs(2),
    hasArgument(0, ignoringImplicit(declRefExpr().bind("lhs"))),
    hasArgument(1, ignoringImplicit(declRefExpr().bind("rhs"))));

// Eager shape: VarDecl initializer IS the operator call (modulo implicit glue).
auto eager_init = ignoringImplicit(or_call);

// Lazy shape: VarDecl initializer is a CXXMemberCallExpr (operator qbool())
// whose implicit object is the operator| CXXOperatorCallExpr.
// NOTE: drop the cxxConstructExpr layer — Clang does not emit one here.
auto lazy_init = ignoringImplicit(
    cxxMemberCallExpr(on(ignoringImplicit(or_call))));

auto pattern = varDecl(
    hasType(cxxRecordDecl(hasName("qbool"))),
    hasInitializer(anyOf(eager_init, lazy_init))
).bind("var");

Rationale differences vs plan:
 - No cxxConstructExpr in lazy chain (Clang emits ImplicitCastExpr
   <UserDefinedConversion> directly, not a construct expr).
 - `on(...)` binds the implicit object of the member call; that subtree
   is exactly where ignoringImplicit peels the NoOp cast and the
   MaterializeTemporaryExpr to reach the operator call.
 - Binding names unchanged ("lhs", "rhs", "var"); OrCallback::run
   needs no edit. Plan invariant preserved.

title: pow_mod: investigate residual O(W^2) ancilla peak (2W^2+4W+11)

The W^2 term comes from per-iteration witness/lt_flags matrices inherited from the Beat D-A/D-B primitives (kMaxN^2 qbool/BitProxy slots in the stack-budget comment in include/sturm/detail/lib/pow_mod_dsl.hpp).

Consequence: peak ancilla exceeds orkan's 17-qubit simulator budget for every W >= 1, forcing APPEND-mode capture + classical replay for all pow_mod tests. Cap-lift (sturm-3sfl.4) raised kMaxN to 64 only because stack budget, not qubit budget, is the binding constraint.

TODO: investigate whether the residual W^2 term can be reduced — likely candidates:
  - batch lt_flags at the pow_mod layer (option (ii) deferred in sturm-3sfl.3) instead of per-iteration absorb
  - share witness matrices across the W iterations of mul_mod_inplace / square_mod
  - or accept the W^2 ancilla as fundamental and document it as the new floor

Goal of this issue is investigation + decision, not necessarily a rewrite. If reducible, file follow-up beat. If fundamental, update docs/01_principles.md and the pow_mod_dsl.hpp comment to state O(W^2) ancilla as the documented bound (the current comment frames the rewrite as O(W), which is true only of the register topology, not peak ancilla).

Refs:

  - include/sturm/detail/lib/pow_mod_dsl.hpp (cap-lift comment)

title: pow-mod-rewrite: rewrite lib_pow_mod_dsl on D-A + D-B (Beat D-C)
description:
Rewrite lib_pow_mod_dsl (and its __lib_pow_mod_dsl_adj sibling) to use a single accumulator + single squaring register, lowering qubit cost from O(W^2) to O(W), built on Beat D-A (lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl) and Beat D-B (lib_square_mod_dsl).

New algorithm shape:
  acc_reg: W qubits, initialized to 1
  sq_reg:  W qubits, initialized to base

  for i = 0..W-1:
      if exp_bits[i]: lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl(sq_reg, acc_reg, n)        # Beat D-A
      if i < W-1:     lib_square_mod_dsl(sq_reg, n)                       # Beat D-B

  r_bits ^= acc_reg

  # Uncompute: reverse loop with adjoint primitives
  for i = W-1..0:
      if i < W-1:     __lib_square_mod_dsl_adj(sq_reg, n)
      if exp_bits[i]: __lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl_adj(sq_reg, acc_reg, n)

  # Final: zero acc_reg (back to 1) + sq_reg (back to base) -> release

Replaces the existing chain-style implementation in include/sturm/detail/lib/pow_mod_dsl.hpp (sq_chain[W][W] + acc_chain[W+1][W]).

Public sturm::pow_mod (qint_modular.hpp) signature unchanged. Existing tests (tests/lib/test_pow_mod_dsl.cpp, test_pow_mod_dsl_adjoint.cpp, plus the public wrapper tests) must pass unchanged.

Total internal qubits (qualitative): acc_reg (W) + sq_reg (W) + Beat D-A internal (~3W + O(1)) + Beat D-B internal (~3W + O(1) — but only one of A/B is live at a time per loop iteration). Peak: ~5W + O(1). Confirm with live-qubit counter test.

lt_flags batching decision: Beat D-A and Beat D-B may emit per-call lt_flags (from inherited even-n Beat B cascade). Beat D-C must decide whether to:
  (i) absorb them inside each per-iteration call (each forward-then-adjoint pair clears its own lt_flags before returning) — simplest, marginally more qubit-traffic; OR
  (ii) batch at the pow_mod layer — keep a (W * (W-1))-bit lt_flags region live across all W iterations and clean in the reverse pass.
Recommend (i) for V1: simpler accounting, the per-iteration adjoint already runs in step 5 of D-A and D-B's own design, and the qubit savings of (ii) are modest since the inner W-1 cascade dominates anyway. Reconsider only if (i) blows the simulator-qubit budget.

Downstream effect: lift the W cap inside lib_pow_mod_dsl (analogous to how Beat C lifted kMaxN in lib_mul_mod_dsl). That cap-lift is split out into Beat D-D (sturm-3sfl.4); keep this issue focused on the rewrite itself.

Layering: per PRD §4 'no new gate emission'. Built strictly on Beat D-A + Beat D-B. No new arithmetic kernel.

Tests (worker handles inline, mirroring sturm-a5te):
  - n==0 no-op
  - 0^0 == 1 convention
  - W=2 single classical case (e.g. 2^3 mod 5 == 3)
  - W=2 exhaustive sweep
  - W=3 random sweep including even n
  - adjoint round-trip
  - ancilla counter (peak ~5W + O(1))
  - pool live-count round-trip
  - squaring-aliasing case: sq_reg passed to lib_square_mod_dsl is its own register, so this is the natural call shape — tested by the rewrite's own loop.

title: square-mod-dsl: lib_square_mod_dsl + adjoint (Beat D-B)
description:
Add lib-level in-place modular squaring primitive plus its sibling adjoint, analogous to Beat B's lib_double_mod_dsl:

  lib_square_mod_dsl(x_bits, n_bits, n, ...)
    x := (x^2) mod n

This is NOT lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl(x, x, n) — that aliasing case is exactly what's blocked by the lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot distinct-operand precondition (the XOR-copy a -> shifted_reg breaks the alias only if a and shifted_reg are physically distinct from the start, but the in-place dest IS the source for squaring).

Squaring is a 2-to-1 map for n > 1 (x and n-x map to the same x^2), so it is fundamentally non-injective. Per docs/design_even_n_double_mod.md §6: lib_square_mod_dsl "is also non-injective (x and n−x map to the same x²). It will need its own 'lt_flag-equivalent' output, but the analysis is separate from the doubling one."

This issue's deliverable includes deciding the squaring construction. Two endpoints to evaluate:

(a) **Out-of-place + swap + adjoint-uncompute.** Same shape as Beat D-A:
    1. Allocate W-bit r_reg.
    2. Compute r_reg <- x^2 mod n via a fresh out-of-place squaring kernel.
    3. Swap x <-> r_reg.
    4. Uncompute r_reg via adjoint of the squaring kernel.
    The fresh squaring kernel can be a Häner-Roetteler-Svore-style schoolbook multiply specialized for a==b, OR can be implemented as lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot(x, copy_of_x, n, r_reg) where copy_of_x is a fresh W-bit register XOR-copied from x. The latter requires an explicit pre-copy of x, paying W extra qubits to break the alias. Total: ~3W + Beat C internals.

(b) **Direct reversible squaring kernel.** A dedicated reversible squaring algorithm. HRS "Optimizing Quantum Circuits for Arithmetic" describes Karatsuba and schoolbook variants; specialization to squaring saves roughly half the partial products. Investigate during implementation.

Pick (a) for V1 unless (b) is clearly cheaper. (a) gets us O(W) qubits at this layer with minimal new-code surface.

Inherited bits from Beat D-B's reduction: per the design doc §6, "two sources of escape information stack at the squaring layer: (1) inherited (W−1) doubling lt_flags per inner mul_mod call, and (2) endemic (the squaring's own reduction may produce additional comparison bits)." Beat D-B must:
  - Account for the inherited (W−1)-bit lt_flags register from the inner lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot call.
  - Identify and account for any new endemic bits from the squaring reduction (if any — strategy (a) above inherits Beat C's reduction wholesale, so likely none new).
  - Decide whether to (i) tear them down inside the call (paying adjoint cost twice) or (ii) batch them at the pow_mod layer (Beat D-C). Recommend (ii) for budget.

Mandatory adjoint __lib_square_mod_dsl_adj in include/sturm/detail/lib/square_mod_dsl_adj.hpp, paired strictly with the forward call (no algebraic square-root, since squaring is non-injective). Document precondition: "input was produced by a forward call; this is gate-reverse uncomputation."

No public wrapper at this beat — kept private under detail/lib/. Beat D-C will lower lib_pow_mod_dsl onto this primitive together with Beat D-A.

Layering: per PRD §4 'no new gate emission'. Built on lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot + the existing alias-break / swap patterns. No new arithmetic kernel beyond combining existing primitives.

Tests (worker handles inline, mirroring sturm-wdas):
  - n==0 no-op
  - W=2 single classical case
  - W=2 exhaustive sweep over (x, n) with n in [1, 2^W), including the (n+1)/2 type case
  - W=3 random sweep including even n
  - x==0 and x==n-1 edge cases (both square to specific known values)
  - adjoint round-trip
  - ancilla counter (peak ~3W + O(1))
  - pool live-count round-trip
  - lt_flags threading round-trip

title: mul-mod-inplace-dsl: lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl + adjoint (Beat D-A)
description:
Add lib-level in-place modular multiplication primitive plus its sibling adjoint, analogous to Beat A's lib_add_mod_inplace_dsl:

  lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl(a_bits, dest_bits, n_bits, n, ...)
    dest := (dest * a) mod n

Today's lib_mul_mod_dsl (post-Beat C, on lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot) is out-of-place: it produces a fresh result register r and the caller XOR-copies into the destination. The in-place variant skips the explicit XOR-copy and uses dest directly as the carrier, reusing the established compute-into-scratch-then-swap pattern.

Mandatory adjoint sibling __lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl_adj computing dest := (dest * a^{-1}) mod n if a is invertible mod n — but per the Beat D design notes (see sturm-3sfl design block §1) a is NOT generally invertible, so the adjoint cannot rely on multiplicative inverse. Probable resolution: pair the adjoint strictly with its forward call, mirroring the Beat B / sturm-wdas adjoint precondition pattern — "the input was produced by a forward call; uncomputation is gate-reverse, not algebraic inverse." Document precondition explicitly.

Algorithm shape (in-place via scratch + swap + adjoint-uncompute):
  1. Allocate W-bit scratch r_reg.
  2. Run lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot(a_bits, dest_bits, n_bits, n, r_reg)  // r_reg <- (a * dest) mod n
  3. Swap dest_bits <-> r_reg  // qubit-relabel via non-owning views OR three-CNOT swap; pick during impl
  4. Now dest_bits holds (a * dest_old) mod n; r_reg holds dest_old.
  5. Uncompute r_reg via the adjoint of oneshot — open question: oneshot's adjoint expects the ORIGINAL b (= dest_old), which is what r_reg holds, so the adjoint can run with (a_bits, r_reg as b, n_bits, dest_bits as r) and clean both r_reg and the doubling lt_flags. Resolve precise wiring during impl. Net peak: ~3W + Beat C internals.

Note: 2W qubits at this layer (Beat C's ~3W internal + 2W here for in-place) is acceptable per the Beat D design block §1: "keep a W-bit scratch register live, accept ~2W qubits at this layer. Still O(W), still a big win, but not strictly minimal."

Even-n inheritance: per docs/design_even_n_double_mod.md §6, lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot now exposes a (W-1)-bit lt_flags register from the doubling cascade. lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl must thread these correctly per call (one register live across the forward+adjoint pair, deallocated after the adjoint cleanup, OR exposed as an output for the pow_mod layer to batch). Decide during implementation; design notes recommend exposing as output for pow_mod-layer batching.

Mandatory adjoint __lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl_adj in include/sturm/detail/lib/mul_mod_inplace_dsl_adj.hpp, mirroring add_mod_inplace_dsl/_adj pairing.

No public wrapper at this beat — kept private under detail/lib/. Beat D-C will lower lib_pow_mod_dsl onto this primitive.

Layering: per PRD §4 'no new gate emission'. Built strictly on lib_mul_mod_dsl_oneshot + the existing XOR-copy / swap patterns. No new arithmetic kernel.

Tests (worker handles inline, mirroring sturm-7cix's child plan):
  - n==0 no-op
  - W=2 single classical case
  - W=2 exhaustive sweep
  - W=3 random sweep
  - squaring-aliasing (a == dest) case — should fail or be documented as forbidden (Beat D-B handles squaring)
  - adjoint round-trip (forward + adjoint = identity on dest)
  - ancilla counter (peak ~3W + O(1))
  - pool live-count round-trip
  - lt_flags threading round-trip (if lt_flags not batched up)

title: cleanup: STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY redefinition warnings across test targets
description:
After sturm-8n73 bumped the project-wide STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY default from 256 to 512 (CMakeLists.txt:23), every test target that declares its own per-target STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256 via target_compile_definitions now produces a -Wmacro-redefined warning at compile time (project add_compile_definitions sets it to 512 first; per-target target_compile_definitions redefines to 256; the per-target define still wins so behavior is unchanged, but the compile output is noisy).

Affected files (by occurrence count):
  - tests/backend/CMakeLists.txt: ~60 targets at STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256
  - tests/lib/CMakeLists.txt: ~30 targets at STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256
  - tests/qtypes/CMakeLists.txt: 6 targets at STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256
  - tests/transpiler/CMakeLists.txt: 1 target at STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256
  - tests/backend/test_end_to_end.cpp:34 has a `#define STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY 256` at source level

Existing pattern that already does it right (silent): tests/control/CMakeLists.txt and tests/lib/CMakeLists.txt:685-686 use `target_compile_options(... PRIVATE -USTURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY -DSTURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=N)` to undef-then-redef, which suppresses the warning.

Cleanup options (pick one in implementation):
  1. Convert every `target_compile_definitions(... STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256)` to the `-U`/`-D` pair via target_compile_options. Mechanical sed-style change; preserves intent (keep a target's pool small even though project default grew).
  2. Drop per-target =256 overrides where the test does not actually need a small pool, since the project default 512 is a strict superset (more headroom, never less). Smaller and more readable, but forfeits the explicit per-target capacity contract — future bumps to the project default would silently grow these targets too.
  3. Hybrid: drop the override where 256 was just "the old default" and the test doesn't depend on the exact value; keep `-U`/`-D` only where the target genuinely needs a specific capacity (e.g. pool-drain tests, capacity-boundary tests).

Hybrid (option 3) is the right call — read each target's intent before stripping. tests/test_qubit_pool.cpp asserts `pool().capacity() == STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY` so it is value-agnostic; targets like test_end_to_end.cpp embed the constant in source and need either a matching CMake define or the source-level #define removed.

Acceptance:
  - Clean build (no -Wmacro-redefined warnings touching STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY).
  - All ctest targets still pass with --parallel 6.
  - No silent capacity reductions: every target that previously had a hard cap below the project default still has one (via -U/-D) unless explicitly judged unnecessary.

HARD LIMIT: --parallel 6 / -j6 only on every cmake/cmake --build/ctest/make/ninja invocation (CLAUDE.md).

title: pow-mod-rewrite: O(W) modular exponentiation (Beat D)
description:
Apply the same in-place trick one level up: collapse lib_pow_mod_dsl's O(W^2) qubit cost to O(W) by introducing in-place modular multiplication primitives and rewriting the chains.

Two new lib-level primitives needed (analogous to Beats A and B for mul):
  - lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl: dest := (dest * a) mod n
  - lib_square_mod_dsl:       x   := (x^2)    mod n   (sidesteps mul_mod's a==b case)

Both lower onto the rewritten lib_mul_mod_dsl (Beat C) plus a single accumulator register.

Then rewrite lib_pow_mod_dsl (and __lib_pow_mod_dsl_adj) on top:
  acc_reg: W qubits, initialized to 1
  sq_reg:  W qubits, initialized to base

  for i = 0..W-1:
      if exp[i]: lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl(sq_reg, acc_reg, n)
      if i < W-1: lib_square_mod_dsl(sq_reg, n)

  r ^= acc_reg
  # Uncompute via adjoint primitives in reverse order

Replaces the existing chain-style implementation in include/sturm/detail/lib/pow_mod_dsl.hpp (sq_chain[W][W] + acc_chain[W+1][W]).

Public sturm::pow_mod signature unchanged. Existing pow_mod tests must pass unchanged.

This beat is OPTIONAL relative to Beat C — Beat C lands the headline mul_mod improvement on its own. Beat D extends the same pattern; can be deferred indefinitely if priorities shift.

HARD LIMIT: All cmake/ctest/make/ninja invocations capped at 6 threads (--parallel 6 / -j6). See CLAUDE.md.
design:
Open design questions for this beat:

1. **lib_mul_mod_inplace_dsl shape.** dest := (dest * a) mod n is harder than the in-place add — multiplication's natural shape is out-of-place into a fresh result. The classical workaround is: compute fresh r = (dest * a) mod n into scratch, swap dest ↔ r, then uncompute scratch (which now holds the old dest value, which we can recover via __lib_mul_mod_dsl_adj using (a, r=new dest) as inputs IF r * a^-1 = old dest mod n, which requires a invertible mod n — NOT generally true). Probable resolution: keep a W-bit scratch register live, accept ~2W qubits at this layer. Still O(W), still a big win, but not strictly minimal. Resolve during implementation.

2. **lib_square_mod_dsl.** Squaring x := x^2 mod n has the same issue magnified — the result depends on x in a non-linear way, so simple swap-and-uncompute doesn't work. Likely needs an out-of-place squaring kernel followed by deallocation of the old x. Investigate published reversible squaring constructions (Häner-Roetteler-Svore covers this).

3. **Test plan.** Mirror sturm-a5te (the original pow_mod issue) children when claiming.

4. **Cap lifting.** Beat C lifts kMaxN for mul_mod; Beat D should similarly lift the W cap inside pow_mod once internal qubit count is O(W).

5. **Schedule.** This beat is genuinely deferable — Beat C lands the qubit-budget win for the most common use case (raw modular multiplication). Beat D is primarily relevant if pow_mod is on a critical path for users; if it isn't, defer.

title: LO-2 backend: replace classical-only *_oop wrappers with reversible gate networks
description:
Umbrella epic. The LO-2 transpiler emits calls to mul_oop / and_oop / or_oop / divide_oop (and *_oop_adj counterparts) as the runtime targets for desugared compound-assign operations on qint_t<W>. divide_oop already has a real reversible implementation in include/sturm/qtypes/divide_oop.hpp, but mul_oop / and_oop / or_oop in include/sturm/qtypes/lossy_oop.hpp are classical-only placeholders: they update tmp.value / tmp.super_mask but emit no gates and leave tmp.qubits at the default-constructed -1 sentinel. Same for all four *_oop_adj helpers (mul/and/or/divide).

This was a deliberate scoping decision in sturm-czfi: the example targets that drove the LO-2 fix (example_qint_arith, example_phase_abc_demo) keep both operands on the classical short-circuit path (qubits[0] < 0 throughout main), so the wrappers only had to honour the classical bookkeeping invariants for the build & run gate to pass. The DSLs that the proper reversible implementations would dispatch into already exist in tree (lib_mul_dsl, lib_c_and_dsl, lib_or_dsl, with adjoint registrations now extracted into *_dsl_adj.hpp siblings via sturm-nmf1). The missing piece is connective tissue between the wrapper and the DSL.

REFERENCE: include/sturm/qtypes/divide_oop.hpp is the worked example for what each wrapper should look like (qubit allocation, dispatch into the matching lib_*_dsl, STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT pairing).

CHILDREN:
- mul_oop / mul_oop_adj — drive lib_mul_dsl
- and_oop / and_oop_adj — drive c_and_dsl (Toffoli per bit)
- or_oop / or_oop_adj — drive or_dsl (De Morgan ladder)

ACCEPTANCE (epic-level):
- All three wrappers allocate qubits and emit the matching reversible network when at least one operand has qubits (mirroring the current divide_oop fast-path / classical-path split).
- Adjoints are structural inverses registered via STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT, not classical zeroers.
- example_qint_arith and example_phase_abc_demo continue to pass on the classical short-circuit path (regression guard on the existing behaviour).
- New tests exercise the gate-emitting path for each of mul / and / or with at least one operand having allocated qubits.
- All build/test commands capped at --parallel 6.

title: Deferred: correct handling of *= upper-W bits and /= discarded remainder under superposition inputs
description: Pre-existing issue noticed while planning sturm-h5it. In qint_t::operator*= the upper W bits of the 2W Cuccaro result are released unconditionally (qint_arith_v3.hpp:113), and in operator/= the remainder register is released unconditionally (qint_arith_v3.hpp:141). This is safe only when the inputs A and B are in computational-basis states; with superposition inputs those registers are entangled with A/B and releasing them silently discards quantum information. Out of scope for the current in-place-under-WHEN fix (sturm-h5it) per user decision. File here for later work: likely needs Bennett-style uncomputation or explicit documentation that *= / /= require classical operands.
notes: Superseded by sturm-lggp (sturm-lo epic): MUL_UPPER_W and DIV_REMAINDER discoverability tags retired with garbage_registry.hpp deletion in sturm-pw2f (LO-4). Compile-time LO desugar handles upper-W and remainder cleanup via invert(lib_mul_dsl)/invert(lib_div_dsl) at scope exit.

title: Deferred: transpiler pass to consume garbage_registry and emit uncomputation at WHEN scope exit

This issue tracks: a transpiler pass / runtime hook at WHEN scope exit that walks the per-scope garbage records registered during the scope body and emits an appropriate uncomputation sequence so the garbage qubits return to |0> and can be released cleanly. Requires figuring out the uncomputation scheme per op tag (AND/OR are self-inverse XOR but rely on the now-overwritten inputs; MUL/DIV/MOD need dedicated reverse DSLs or Bennett-style saved-copies). Not in scope for the current session; file now to anchor the future work.

title: Bug: glue_fixture_plugins build fails — duplicate pm4.demo.tag registration aborts clang
description:
Surfaced by the Phase N autopilot final-suite run (2026-04-23). Build target glue_fixture_plugins fails with a clang frontend abort:

  sturm-transpile plugin: duplicate op registration for kind_id 'pm4.demo.tag' (second registration rejected)
  ...
  7  libsturm-transpile-plugin.so  sturm::transpile::plugin::Registry::register_op(...) + 207
  8  libsturm-transpile-plugin.so  sturm_register_plugin_v1 + 121
  9  libsturm-transpile-plugin.so  sturm::transpile::pm4_link_demo::LinkTimeDemoPlugin::register_all(Registry&) const + 25
  ...
  clang++-17: error: clang frontend command failed with exit code 134

Root cause: examples/plugin_demo's PM4 demo plugin registers op kind 'pm4.demo.tag' twice:
  1. Statically linked into libsturm-transpile-plugin.so (STURM_REGISTER_PLUGIN static init path).
  2. Dynamically loaded via -Xclang -plugin-arg-sturm-transpile -Xclang load=.../libsturm-pm4-demo-plugin.so.

Registry::register_op treats the duplicate as fatal and abort()s inside the clang frontend.

This is a PM4-era artifact (plugin_demo last touched in sturm-4oyr.8 / PM4-7 — f1945b8). The ctest tests that drive this pathway (test_cmake_plugins_run, test_cmake_glue_run) both PASS in the final ctest run; the failure is only in the build target glue_fixture_plugins whose purpose seems to be a compile-check fixture that nothing consumes.

Repro: cmake --build build --parallel 6 --target glue_fixture_plugins

Options: (a) make Registry::register_op tolerate duplicate registrations from the same library (current behaviour: fatal abort); (b) remove the static STURM_REGISTER_PLUGIN in the PM4 demo plugin so it only loads dynamically; (c) remove glue_fixture_plugins from the default all-target if nothing depends on it.

title: SturmTranspile.cmake hardcodes STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256 in libclang --extra-arg
description:
cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake:122 passes a literal "--extra-arg=-DSTURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256" to the sturm-transpile invocation. If a user configures STURM with -DSTURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=N (N != 256), the compile step sees the overridden N (via add_compile_definitions in top-level CMakeLists.txt), but the transpiler's libclang frontend still parses the source tree with STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=256. This can produce divergent macro-driven template instantiations between the transpile pass and the compile pass.

Discovered while validating PL-1 (sturm-flli) acceptance: the installed sturmConfig.cmake now correctly propagates the chosen capacity to consumers via INTERFACE_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS, which highlighted that SturmTranspile.cmake itself is the last place still hardcoding 256.

Scope
-----
Replace the literal 256 in cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake with ${STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY} (in-tree) and the configure-time value baked through sturmConfig.cmake.in (installed). Verify both paths: in-tree build with -DSTURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=512 produces a transpile step that sees 512, and an installed find_package(sturm) consumer does the same.

Acceptance
----------
- In-tree: grep -F '"--extra-arg=-DSTURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=${STURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY}"' cmake/SturmTranspile.cmake succeeds (or equivalent).
- Configure with -DSTURM_ANCILLA_CAPACITY=512 and trace one add_quantum_executable call — transpile --extra-arg shows 512.
- Out-of-tree find_package(sturm REQUIRED) consumer sees the same 512 on the transpile step.
- Regression: full ctest green at the default (256).

title: Phase L PL-7 (stretch): packaging/docker/Dockerfile + GHCR publish workflow
description:
Stretch deliverable enumerated in the Phase L roadmap "options" table but NOT in the core Deliverables list. Provides a zero-install path for users who already run Docker. Lower priority than PL-1..PL-6 — can ship in v0.1.1 if it slips.

Files
-----
1. packaging/docker/Dockerfile — multi-stage build:

   Stage 1 (builder):
     FROM ubuntu:24.04 AS build
     RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
         llvm-17-dev libclang-17-dev clang-17 cmake git ca-certificates
     COPY . /src
     WORKDIR /src
     RUN cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
         -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/sturm \
         -DLLVM_DIR=/usr/lib/llvm-17/lib/cmake/llvm \
         -DClang_DIR=/usr/lib/llvm-17/lib/cmake/clang && \
         cmake --build build -j && \
         cmake --install build

   Stage 2 (runtime):
     FROM ubuntu:24.04
     RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
         libclang-cpp17 libllvm17 && \
         rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
     COPY --from=build /opt/sturm /opt/sturm
     ENV PATH="/opt/sturm/bin:${PATH}"
     ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/sturm/bin/sturm-transpile"]

2. docker-publish job added to .github/workflows/release.yml (or a sibling workflow docker-publish.yml):
   - `docker/build-push-action` pushing to:
       ghcr.io/soerenwilkening/sturm-transpile:v${VERSION}
       ghcr.io/soerenwilkening/sturm-transpile:latest
   - Authenticated via GITHUB_TOKEN + packages:write permission.
   - Triggered on the same v* tag events as release.yml.

3. README.md addition (appended to the Install section):
     **Docker:**
     ```
     docker run -v $PWD:/w ghcr.io/soerenwilkening/sturm-transpile:latest /w/src.cpp \
       --output-dir /w/out --extra-arg=-I/opt/sturm/include --extra-arg=-std=c++20
     ```

Acceptance

- Image size < 500 MB (measure with `docker images ghcr.io/soerenwilkening/sturm-transpile`).
- `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w ghcr.io/soerenwilkening/sturm-transpile:v0.1.0 /w/tests/smoke/minimal_or.cpp --output-dir /w/out --extra-arg=-I/opt/sturm/include --extra-arg=-std=c++20` transpiles a mounted source file; the generated file contains uncompute_or.

title: Phase T §9 deferrals — non-critical future transpiler reversibility work
description:
Tracks four reversibility-related extensions that Phase T (epic sturm-xrob, closed 2026-04-24) explicitly deferred per PRD §9. None are critical at the moment — Phase T closed green with 314/314 tests passing inside the documented shape envelope — but each represents a real gap in the auto-synthesis pipeline that will need to be addressed when the corresponding use case lands.

**Scope of deferrals** (all roadmap-noted in docs/roadmap_transpiler_post_mvp.md Phase T completion blockquote):

1. **Recursion** — self-calls inside a [[clang::annotate(\"sturm::reversible\")]] forward. Currently Q-A twin synth + R-A adjoint emission do not handle a forward calling itself; naive emission would recurse into the un-synthesised adjoint. Requires either a fixed-point emission strategy or an explicit base-case contract.

2. **Cross-TU synthesis** — forward defined in one translation unit, sturm::invert(&fn) call site in another. PI-1's invert-call scanner + T-2's three-condition gate (PRD §9 Q2) operate at end-of-TU; a cross-TU invert call cannot see the forward's annotation at synth time. Requires either a link-time synthesis pass, an export/import manifest, or forcing all reversible forwards into headers with inline semantics.

3. **Member functions** — class methods annotated reversible. The current matcher pipeline assumes free functions: Q-A twin synth constructs __fn_out at global scope, R-B emits STURM_REGISTER_ADJOINT(fn, __fn_adj) with fully-qualified names. Member functions introduce implicit 'this', access control, and class-template-specialisation complications that none of the current matchers handle.

4. **Templates** — template-dependent reversible forwards (e.g., template<int N> void fn(qint<N>&)). Synth is currently driven at AST-parse time per concrete FunctionDecl; template instantiations only produce concrete FDs on-demand. Requires either lazy instantiation-time synthesis or eager all-instantiations synthesis (with associated combinatorial cost).

**Status:** Backlog. No implementation planned. File child bd issues when a concrete use case motivates tackling any of these four.

**References:**
- PRD §9 (locked decisions around reversibility scope)
- docs/roadmap_transpiler_post_mvp.md — Phase T completion blockquote (2026-04-24 entry)
- Closed epic sturm-xrob (Phase T — Transpiler integration of automatic adjoint synthesis)

File child bd issues against that document when concrete use cases land.

Phase I output-param classification (classify_output in transpiler/src/matcher_common.hpp) emits four verdicts: Intermediate (VarDecl in call's enclosing scope or descendant -> uncompute at scope exit), IntermediateOuter (ancestor scope still inside the function -> uncompute at declaring scope's close brace via insert_before_override), Final (function param or namespace/file scope -> NO uncompute, NO diagnostic, escapes), SkipWithDiagnostic (declared outside loop/branch/WHEN but mutated inside -> skip_uncompute=true + stderr diagnostic, mirrors PH-3). Multi-output conservative-skip rule: if ANY output is SkipWithDiagnostic OR Final, the entire call is skipped (cannot partially invert a multi-output routine). NEVER run many clang/compiler commands in parallel or in rapid sequence — user had to force-restart their Mac after dozens of clang invocations ran at once during a beads session. Rule: (1) run build/compile steps via a single cmake/make invocation with a BOUNDED -j flag (max -j2 on this machine, never unlimited), (2) never spawn parallel Bash tool calls that each run clang/clang++, (3) never loop over many source files calling the compiler directly — use the build system, (4) if a test harness would compile many files, run it serially and confirm with the user before kicking off. === Header dependency graph (input to B0 / sturm-65rs.5) ===

CURRENT (one-way):
  qint_alias.hpp  --(includes)-->  qint_fwd.hpp
  qint_fwd.hpp:    declares `template<size_t Width=64> class qint_t;` and
                   `using qint = qint_t<64>;`. No `#include "qint_alias.hpp"`.

TARGET (after B1 flips alias):
  qint_fwd.hpp:    declares qint_t<W> forward, then INCLUDES qint_alias.hpp,
                   then `using qint = ::sturm::frontend::qint;`
  qint_alias.hpp:  still includes qint_fwd.hpp (needs the qint_t<W> forward decl
                   for the templated converting ctor `qint(const qint_t<W>&)`).

CYCLE TRACE (acyclicity proof):
  Step 1: TU includes qint_fwd.hpp.
    - `#pragma once` guard on qint_fwd.hpp set.
    - Forward decl `template <size_t Width=64> class qint_t;` emitted.
    - `#include "qint_alias.hpp"` reached.
  Step 2: qint_alias.hpp processed.
    - `#pragma once` guard on qint_alias.hpp set.
    - `#include "qint_fwd.hpp"` (line 44 today) — NO-OP under #pragma once.
    - Class `frontend::qint` defined; references `::sturm::qint_t<W>` only via
      the forward decl emitted in step 1 (the class body's converting ctor at
      line 144 is a DECLARATION; the inline definition at line 203 never
      dereferences `src`, so a forward declaration is sufficient — the body
      compiles without the full qint_t<W> definition).
  Step 3: Control returns to qint_fwd.hpp.
    - `using qint = ::sturm::frontend::qint;` emitted (referencing the now-
      complete frontend::qint type).

ACYCLICITY VERDICT: Safe under #pragma once + the property that qint_alias.hpp
needs only the qint_t<W> forward declaration, never the full definition. The
inclusion order INSIDE qint_fwd.hpp is load-bearing and MUST be:
  (i) #pragma once
  (ii) `template<size_t Width=64> class qint_t;` (forward decl)
  (iii) `#include "sturm/qtypes/qint_alias.hpp"`
  (iv) `using qint = ::sturm::frontend::qint;` (in namespace sturm)

If the include order were inverted ((iii) before (ii)), qint_alias.hpp would
re-enter qint_fwd.hpp's #pragma once guard with NO qint_t<W> forward decl
available, and `qint(const ::sturm::qint_t<W>&)` would fail to parse.

This pattern — forward decl, then include the consumer, then define the alias —
matches the canonical "wedge" header pattern in the codebase (mirrors how
qbool.hpp wedges qint_compare.hpp through qbool_fwd.hpp). No existing test
includes qint_alias.hpp WITHOUT going through qint_fwd.hpp first; B1's new
test (sturm-65rs.6, plan §7) will pin compile-success of `#include

sturm.hpp umbrella does NOT expose qbool operators. It pulls only uncompute/uncompute_api.hpp (which brings qbool.hpp, the record def) and routines/invert.hpp. To actually compile `a OR b` / `a AND b` / `a XOR b` on qbool you need ONE of: (1) STURM_BACKEND_ENABLED=1 + include sturm/control/when.hpp (the examples/or_circuit.cpp pattern; when.hpp transitively pulls qbool_logic.hpp / qbool_ops.hpp), OR (2) explicit include sturm/qtypes/qbool_ops.hpp (backend path, emits 3-gate OR), OR (3) explicit include sturm/qtypes/qbool_logic.hpp (gated on ifndef STURM_BACKEND_ENABLED — eager frontend). Plain `include sturm/sturm.hpp` + `using sturm::qbool;` + `a bitor b` will produce an unresolved-operator error — which sturm-transpile silently swallows via IgnoringDiagConsumer, leaving a pass-through file with no uncompute_*(...) injection.

Transpiler MVP matcher (transpiler/src/matcher.cpp:162) uses hasInitializer(cxxOperatorCallExpr(...)) and only matches the eager qbool operator| (qbool_logic.hpp:26). Under STURM_BACKEND_ENABLED, operator| on qbool returns OrExpr<qbool> (lazy_expr.hpp:88), materialized via OrExpr::operator qbool() (qbool_ops.hpp:203). The init AST then becomes CXXConstructExpr -> CXXMemberCallExpr -> CXXOperatorCallExpr, which the current matcher does not traverse, so no uncompute_or is injected in backend-compiled TUs like examples/or_circuit.cpp. Fix would be ignoringImplicit + peel through cxxMemberCallExpr/cxxConstructExpr, plus a fixture with STURM_BACKEND_ENABLED. Punt accepted: lazy expressions will be eliminated later.
